questions.question: In what case will the driver make a forced stop?

answers.text: Stopping just before a crosswalk to give way to a pedestrian
Stopped on the roadway due to a technical malfunction of the vehicle
In both of the above cases

questions.comment: “Forced stop” is the cessation of movement of a vehicle due to its technical malfunction, the danger created by the cargo being transported, the condition of the driver (passenger) or the appearance of an obstacle on the road. (Clause 1.2 of the Traffic Regulations, the term “Forced stop”)

questions.question: Are you allowed to turn onto a dirt road?

answers.text: Allowed only in case of technical malfunction of the vehicle

questions.comment: Ahead in the direction of your movement is warning sign 1.11.2 “Dangerous turn” and signs 1.34.2 “Direction of turn”, which indicate the direction of movement on a curved road with a small radius with limited visibility. There is nothing that would prohibit you from turning onto a dirt road. At your request, turn right (“Road signs”).

questions.question: Can you stop at the designated location to pick up a passenger?

answers.text: Yes, if you drive a taxi

questions.comment: Sign 3.28 “Parking prohibited” does not prohibit stopping. You can stop at the indicated place. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Which of the following signs prohibit the movement of moped drivers?
questions.comment: All of the following signs prohibit the movement of moped drivers: A – 4.4.1 “Bicycle path”; B – 5.14.1 “Lane for route vehicles”; B – 4.5.2 “Pedestrian and bicycle path with combined traffic”; D – 4.5.4 “Pedestrian and bicycle path with separation of traffic.” (Road signs) Only sign 5.14.2 “Lane for cyclists” allows the movement of mopeds, but it is not presented in the question Paragraph 24.7 of the Traffic Rules

questions.question: You intend to turn left. Where should you stop to give way to a car?

answers.text: Before the intersection at the marking line
At an intersection before a broken line

questions.comment: According to sign 2.4 “Give way”, drivers must give way to vehicles moving along the road being crossed. Marking 1.13 in the form of triangles indicates the place where you should stop if necessary. You have such a need, because when turning left you give way to a passenger car. (“Road signs”, “Horizontal markings”)

questions.question: What does a flashing green traffic light mean?

answers.text: Warns of a malfunction of the traffic light
Allows movement and informs that a prohibitory signal will soon be turned on

questions.comment: The blinking duration of a green traffic light is usually 3-4 seconds. This allows the driver to make a decision in advance, depending on specific conditions: 1) continue driving at the same speed; 2) increase the speed slightly; 3) begin reducing the speed until stopping. (Clause 6.2 of the Traffic Rules)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: The driver is required to give signals with the direction indicators (by hand):

answers.text: In all of the above cases

questions.comment: Before starting to move, change lanes, turn (U-turn) and stop, the driver is required to give signals with turn signals in the appropriate direction, and if they are missing or faulty, with his hand. When performing a maneuver, there should not be a danger to traffic or interference with other road users. (Clause 8.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: What should you do when turning right?

answers.text: Change into the right lane, then make a turn
Continue in the second lane until the intersection, then turn

questions.comment: The markings allow right turns from both lanes, so both options are possible. In such cases, when making a turn at an intersection, follow the lane you have chosen. (“Horizontal markings” 1.18, paragraph 8.5 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Which trajectory are you allowed to reverse?
questions.comment: Departure from the intersection of roadways must be done on “your” side, i.e. based on right-hand traffic without going to the side of oncoming traffic. Moving along trajectory “B”, you are making oncoming traffic on the road you are crossing, which is extremely dangerous, as you can make a head-on collision with a car approaching from the left. You should turn around along the trajectory “A”. (Clause 8.6 of traffic rules)

questions.question: At what speed can you continue driving outside a populated area in the left lane in a passenger car?

answers.text: Not less than 50 km/h and not more than 70 km/h
Not less than 50 km/h and not more than 90 km/h

questions.comment: Above the left lane hangs sign 4.6 “Minimum speed limit” with sign 8.14 “Traffic lane” indicating the lane covered by the sign. The speed in the left lane should not be less than 50 km/h and should not exceed the speed limit for passenger cars outside populated areas, i.e. no more than 90 km/h (“Road signs”, paragraph 10.3 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Is it possible for a passenger car driver to outrun trucks outside a populated area along such a trajectory?

answers.text: It is possible if the speed of trucks is less than 30 km/h

questions.comment: On dual carriageway roads with four or more lanes, overtaking is prohibited. In such situations, you can only advance. By observing the rules of maneuvering, the driver of a passenger car on this section of the road can advance any vehicles along various trajectories, including the one indicated. (Clause 9.2 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: In what case is the driver allowed to park the car in the specified place?

answers.text: Only if the distance to the solid marking line is at least 3 m
Only if the distance to the edge of the roadway being crossed is at least 5 m
If both of the above conditions are met

questions.comment: The driver does not violate the rules of stopping and parking. The distance to the edge of the roadway and to the continuous marking line is maintained - no less than acceptable. Stopping and parking behind a pedestrian crossing is also acceptable. The correct answer is if both of the above conditions are met. (Clause 12.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: When turning right you must give way to:
questions.comment: When turning right or left, the driver is obliged to give way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway on which he is turning, persons using personal mobility devices (hereinafter referred to as SIM) and cyclists, regardless of whether it is a controlled or unregulated intersection. (Clause 13.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to drive straight through the intersection. Who should you give way to?
questions.comment: The intersection is equal. Under equal conditions, trams have an advantage over trackless vehicles. They are guided by the “right hand rule” among themselves. There is an obstacle on the right side of tram "A". Accordingly, tram “B” passes first, followed by “A”, you are the last. (Clause 13.11 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Who do you have to give way to when turning left?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles on the main road have priority, and drivers follow the “right-hand rule” among themselves. Without yielding to anyone, you pass first, the bus second, the passenger car last, since it is on a secondary road. (“Road signs”, paragraphs 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: At what maximum speed can you continue following the sign?
questions.comment: In the residential area, according to the sign you are entering, driving at a speed of no more than 20 km/h is allowed (“Road signs” 5.21, paragraph 10.2 of the traffic rules).

questions.question: To transport people on a motorcycle, the driver must have a driver's license to drive the following vehicles:

answers.text: Any category or subcategory for 2 or more years
Only category “A” or subcategory “A1” for 2 or more years

questions.comment: Transportation of people on a motorcycle must be carried out by a driver who has a driver’s license for the right to drive a vehicle of category “A” or subcategory “A1” for 2 or more years. (Clause 22.2(1) of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: What kind of malfunction is the vehicle allowed to operate?

answers.text: Fuel tank shut-off devices do not work
The driver's seat adjustment mechanism and locking device do not work
The windshield defogger does not work

questions.comment: The malfunctions listed in the answers, with the exception of the inoperative window lift, are indicated in the "List of malfunctions". The inoperative window lift is not indicated in this list. Consequently, this cannot be a reason to prohibit the operation of the vehicle. ("List of malfunctions" cl. 8.3, 9.2)
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: In the case when the right wheels of the car run over an unimproved wet shoulder, it is recommended:

answers.text: Brake and come to a complete stop
Brake and smoothly steer the car onto the roadway
Without braking, smoothly steer the car onto the roadway

questions.comment: This situation is dangerous due to the occurrence of a moment of force that tends to turn the car around. Try to smoothly return the car to the roadway without changing speed.

questions.question: What is meant by driver reaction time?

answers.text: Time from the moment the driver detects the danger until the vehicle comes to a complete stop
Time from the moment the driver discovers the danger until the start of taking measures to avoid it
Time required to move your foot from the fuel control pedal to the brake pedal

questions.comment: The reaction time of the driver is understood as the time from the moment the driver detects a danger to the beginning of taking measures to avoid it. The reaction time of the driver is a variable value. It mainly depends on the age, well-being at the moment. It is possible to compensate for the lack of reaction by reducing the speed.("Vehicle Control Technique")

questions.question: How many lanes does this road have?
questions.comment: A median strip divides the road into carriageways. This road has two carriageways, four lanes. (Clause 1.2 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Can you be the first to enter the bridge?

answers.text: It is possible, if you do not impede the movement of an oncoming car

questions.comment: Sign 2.7 “Take advantage of oncoming traffic” gives you the right to be the first to pass through a narrow section of the road, that is, across a bridge. (“Road signs”, paragraph 1.2 term “Give way”)

questions.question: Are you allowed to stop to pick up a passenger?

answers.text: Allowed only on even days of the month
Allowed only on odd days of the month

questions.comment: Sign 3.29 “Parking is prohibited on odd days of the month” only restricts parking. Stopping in its coverage area is not prohibited at any time. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: What is prohibited in the area covered by this sign?

answers.text: Movement of all vehicles at a speed of no more than 20 km/h

questions.comment: Sign 5.33 “Pedestrian zone” designates the place from which the territory (section of the road) begins, on which the movement of only pedestrians and persons equivalent to them is allowed (these are those moving in wheelchairs without a motor, driving a bicycle, moped, motorcycle, carrying a sled, cart, child stroller and wheelchair), as well as cyclists and persons using SIM for movement in the cases established in paragraphs 24.2, 24.3, 24.4 and 24.6 traffic rules. Entry into the designated area and, accordingly, the movement of any mechanical vehicles in it is prohibited. (“Road signs”, the term “Pedestrian” clause 1.2 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Are you allowed to enter a lane with reversible traffic if the reversible traffic light is turned off?

answers.text: Allowed if the bus speed is less than 30 km/h

questions.comment: When the signals of the reverse traffic light, which is located above the lane marked on both sides with markings 1.9, are turned off, entry into this lane is prohibited. (Clause 6.7 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: The information light section in the form of a silhouette of a pedestrian and an arrow with a flashing white-lunar signal, located under the traffic light, informs the driver that:

answers.text: At the pedestrian crossing in the direction of which he is turning, a traffic light is turned on, allowing pedestrians to move
At the pedestrian crossing in the direction of which he is turning, a traffic light is turned on, prohibiting the movement of pedestrians
He turns towards the pedestrian crossing

questions.comment: An information light section in the form of a silhouette of a pedestrian and an arrow with a flashing white-lunar signal, located under the traffic light, informs the driver that at the pedestrian crossing in the direction of which he is turning, a traffic light is turned on, allowing the movement of pedestrians. The direction of the arrow indicates a pedestrian crossing where the traffic light is on, allowing pedestrians to move (clause 6.4).
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: The hand of the driver of a passenger car raised up is a signal informing you of his intention:

answers.text: Slow down to stop and give way to the motorcycle

questions.comment: The driver's warning light does not work, so he is forced to give appropriate hand signals. According to sign 2.4 “Give way,” the motorcyclist has the right of way. A raised hand indicates the intention to slow down in order to give way to a motorcyclist (“Road signs”, paragraph 8.1 of the traffic rules).

questions.question: Moving in the left lane, the driver intends to change lanes to the right. Which of the pictures shows a situation in which he is obliged to give way?
questions.comment: In the left figure, the advantage is given to a car moving in the same lane without changing direction, i.e. from the “owner of the strip.” The driver moving in the left lane gives way. In the right picture there is a simultaneous lane change. Drivers are guided by the “right hand rule”, i.e. whoever has an obstacle on the right concedes. There is interference on the right side of the driver, who is also driving in the left lane. He gives way in this situation as well. (Clause 8.4 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Can you make a U-turn in this place?

answers.text: Only possible if there is no approaching train

questions.comment: A U-turn is prohibited at a railway crossing, the boundaries of which are barriers, and in their absence - signs 1.3.1 “Single-track railway” or 1.3.2 “Multi-track railway”. In our case, a railway crossing without a barrier. You can make a U-turn along the specified trajectory, since you are making it at a safe distance from the railway tracks. (Clause 8.11 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: In what cases is it permissible to drive over broken marking lines dividing the roadway into traffic lanes?

answers.text: Only if there are no other vehicles on the road
Only when driving in the dark
In all of the above cases

questions.comment: It is allowed to drive over broken marking lines only when changing lanes. (Clause 9.7 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: Are you allowed to overtake a motorcycle?

answers.text: Allowed if the motorcycle driver has reduced speed

questions.comment: The intersection is equivalent. At equivalent intersections, overtaking is prohibited for all types of transport by all vehicles. The motorcyclist slows down and gives way to the obstacle on the right. You do the same. Otherwise, you will violate both the overtaking rules and the rules for driving through intersections (Clause 11.4, 13.11 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: Are you allowed to stay at the indicated place?

answers.text: It is allowed if the car is no closer than 5 m from the edge of the intersecting roadway

questions.comment: At a roundabout intersection you can stop and park, but the distance between the stopped vehicle and the edge of the roadway must be at least 5 m (Clause 12.4, 12.5 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: You intend to turn left. Who should you give way to?
questions.comment: The intersection is controlled. Priority signs don't work. When turning left, you give way to a bus moving straight from the opposite direction, and to pedestrians crossing the roadway you are turning onto (Clause 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: In which case do you have an advantage?

answers.text: In both of the above cases

questions.comment: The intersection is equivalent. Drivers are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves, i.e. whoever has an obstacle on the right gives way. You have an advantage both when turning right and when turning left, i.e. in both of these cases (Clause 13.11 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: Is a motorcycle driver required to give way to you?
questions.comment: The motorcyclist enters the road marked with sign 5.1 “Motorway”, which is the main road in relation to the adjacent one. At the intersection of unequal roads, vehicles moving on the main road have priority. The motorcyclist is obliged to give way to you. (Clause 1.2, 13.9 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: Is the driver allowed to pass a truck?

answers.text: It is allowed if the distance between the barrier and a stopped truck is more than 5 m

questions.comment: The driver of a car wants to go around a truck standing in front of a closed barrier. The rules stipulating the procedure for driving through a railway crossing; such a maneuver (with driving into oncoming traffic) is prohibited (Clause 15.3 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: In which of the following cases is towing with a flexible hitch prohibited?

answers.text: Only in the dark and in poor visibility conditions
In all of the above cases

questions.comment: Remember this answer. During the exam they often answer that only on mountain roads. Apparently there is an associated danger associated with heights. The rules prohibit towing with a flexible hitch only in icy conditions (Clause 20.4 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: It is prohibited to operate motor vehicles (category L) if the remaining tire tread depth (in the absence of wear indicators) is no more than:
questions.comment: For motor vehicles belonging to vehicles of categories L, the residual depth of the tire tread pattern (in the absence of wear indicators) should be no more than 0.8 mm (“List of faults”, clause 5.4)
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: Does the anti-lock braking system eliminate the possibility of skidding or drifting when cornering?

answers.text: Completely eliminates the possibility of only skidding
Completely excludes the possibility of demolition only
Does not exclude the possibility of drift or drift

questions.comment: Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) in automobiles are systems equipped with feedback brake control devices that prevent the wheels from locking during braking, thereby maintaining control and directional stability. This system has a “big plus”, but also has a “minus”. If you press the brake pedal quickly (not urgently) on a heterogeneous, even hard road surface, it may work. At the moment it is triggered (from 1 to 2 seconds), the driver cannot influence the braking process. To develop the skill of driving a car when the ABS is activated, perform several “control” braking on a completely free section of the road or territory. When turning a corner, centrifugal force acts on the car. The anti-lock braking system in such situations cannot affect the possibility of drift or skidding.

questions.question: In what cases should cardiopulmonary resuscitation of the victim be started?

answers.text: If you have pain in the heart and difficulty breathing
In the absence of consciousness in the victim, regardless of the presence of breathing
In the absence of consciousness, breathing and blood circulation in the victim

questions.comment: In commenting answers on medical questions, to better remember the correct answer, the technique of “key words” is used, which are highlighted in the text in font. Pay attention to this. The correct answer is if the victim has no consciousness, breathing or blood circulation.

questions.question: When leaving the dirt road at the intersection, you find:

answers.text: On an equivalent road because there are no priority signs
On an equivalent road, since the roadway has a hard surface in front of the intersection

questions.comment: The main one is the paved road in relation to the dirt road. The intersection is unequal. You are on a secondary road, you will exit onto the main road. (Clause 1.2, the term “Main Road”)

questions.question: Where should you stay?

answers.text: Before the edge of the intersecting roadway (B)

questions.comment: If sign 2.5 “Driving without stopping is prohibited” is installed immediately before crossing the roadways, the driver is obliged to stop at the stop line. In its absence (as in this case), the driver is obliged to stop before the border of the roadways, i.e. without going beyond the “B” line. Keep in mind that such places are dangerous and are often “under special control” of traffic police inspectors. Therefore, always fulfill the main condition - a mandatory stop. This will save you from a conflict situation and maintain your own safety. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: You need to drive at a speed of no more than 40 km/h:

answers.text: In all cases when the roadway surface is wet

questions.comment: Plate 8.16 “Wet surface” indicates that the sign applies to the period of time when the roadway surface is wet. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Which of the following signs is installed at the beginning of a one-way road?
questions.comment: Sign “B” - 5.5 “One-way road.” (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Can you stop at this location to pick up or drop off passengers?

answers.text: It is possible, if this does not interfere with the movement of route vehicles

questions.comment: In this case, the stopping place for route vehicles is indicated by a corresponding sign and yellow zigzag markings 1.17.1. Stopping at the indicated place is allowed if you make it to pick up or disembark passengers and at this time do not interfere with the movement of route vehicles or vehicles used as a passenger taxi. (“Road signs”, “Horizontal markings”, clause 12.4 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: When turning right you:

answers.text: You have the right to pass the intersection first
Must give way only to pedestrians
Must give way to a car with a flashing light and a special sound signal on, as well as to pedestrians

questions.comment: The intersection is adjustable. An “operative” with a flashing light and a special sound signal on can deviate from a number of requirements of the Rules. In this situation, all drivers must ensure unhindered passage through the intersection. After passing it, turning right, you also give way to pedestrians. (Clause 3.2, 13.1 of traffic rules)

questions.question: In what cases should a driver not signal with turn signals?

answers.text: Only if there are no other road users on the road
Only if the signal is likely to confuse other road users
In both of the above cases

questions.comment: The signal should be given by direction indicators in advance of the start of the maneuver and terminated immediately after its completion. In this case, the signal should not mislead other road users.(Clause 8.2 of the Traffic Rules)

questions.question: You are allowed to make a right turn:

answers.text: Along any trajectory of the specified

questions.comment: When turning right, the vehicle should move as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway. You have such an opportunity, continue moving along trajectory “A”. (Clause 8.6 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Are you allowed to make a U-turn at an intersection along the specified trajectory?

answers.text: Permitted if road visibility is at least 100 m

questions.comment: There is an intersection ahead. Before making a turn or U-turn on it, it was necessary to change lanes to the left extreme lane. You didn't do this in a timely manner. A U-turn along this trajectory is a violation. (Clause 8.5, 8.8 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: In which lane do you have the right to move at the maximum permitted speed outside the settlement?
questions.comment: The action takes place outside the populated area. In this case, it is prohibited to occupy the left lanes when the right lanes are free. You need to change lanes and continue driving in this situation only in the right lane. (Clause 9.4 of traffic rules)
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: In what case can a driver start overtaking if such a maneuver is not prohibited on a given section of the road?

answers.text: Only if the lane intended for oncoming traffic is clear at a sufficient distance for overtaking
Only if no one overtakes his vehicle

questions.comment: When performing a “classic” overtaking, you must take into account three mandatory conditions, under which, when overtaking, you do not create any interference: 1) oncoming traffic, 2) driving behind, 3) overtaken. (Clause 11.1, 11.2 Traffic Regulations, “Driving Techniques”)

questions.question: Which driver violated the parking rules?
questions.comment: The driver of a passenger car may drive onto the sidewalk adjacent to the roadway only in places marked with sign 6.4 “Parking (parking space)”, with one of the signs 8.6.2, 8.6.3, 8.6.6-8.6.9 “Method of parking a vehicle.” In this situation, there are no such signs, so the driver is a “violator.” The motorcycle driver does not violate the rules of stopping and parking, since the rules prohibit doing this in conditions where the distance between the solid marking line and the stopped vehicle is less than 3 m. Here the action takes place from the side of the broken line, which does not contradict the Rules. (Clause 12.2 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: When driving straight ahead you:

answers.text: Must stop before the stop line
You can continue driving through the intersection without stopping.
Must give way to vehicles coming from other directions

questions.comment: The intersection is controlled. In this case, the priority signs, and these include sign 2.5 “Driving without stopping is prohibited”, according to the principle of priority of traffic regulation, “do not work”, i.e. we are not guided by them. The traffic light is green. Continue driving through the intersection without stopping. (Clause 6.2, 6.15, 13.3 of traffic rules)

questions.question: You intend to turn right. What are your actions?
questions.comment: The intersection is equal. When determining the order of passage through an intersection, drivers are guided by the “right-hand rule,” i.e. whoever has an obstacle on the right gives way. There is no interference on your right when turning right, because... when turning right, your trajectory does not intersect with the motorcycle. Pass the intersection first. (Clause 13.11 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Who do you have to give way to when turning left?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles on the main road have priority; between themselves, trackless vehicles are guided by the “right-hand rule”, yielding to the tram, which has an advantage in equivalent conditions. Tram "A" passes first, you go after it. A passenger car and tram “B” at the same time, since their trajectories do not intersect. (“Road signs”, paragraphs 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Which driver violated the stopping rules?
questions.comment: On the highway, stopping and parking outside of specially designated areas and marked with appropriate signs is prohibited. Both drivers violate the rules. (“Road signs”, paragraphs 12.1, 16.1 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: What equipment should a motor vehicle used for driving instruction have?

answers.text: Additional clutch pedals (except for vehicles with automatic transmission) and brakes
Rear view mirror for driving lessons

questions.comment: The correct answer is all the listed equipment, according to Clause 21.5 of the SDA and Clause 5 of the Tolerance Guidelines
topic: Training riding and additional requirements for the movement of cyclists

questions.question: In what cases is it prohibited to operate a motorcycle?

answers.text: Passenger footrests or handles on the saddle are not rubberized
There is play in the connections between the motorcycle frame and the side trailer frame

questions.comment: Clause 9.8 of the “List of Faults” prohibits the operation of vehicles of category L (motorcycles) if there is play in the connections of the vehicle frame with the frame of the side trailer.
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: When turning a corner, the rear axle of a front-wheel drive vehicle skidded. What are your actions?

answers.text: Reduce the fuel supply, use the steering wheel to stabilize the movement
Slow down and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid
Increase the fuel supply slightly by adjusting the direction of movement with the steering wheel
Significantly increase fuel delivery without changing the steering wheel position

questions.comment: Front-wheel drive cars differ significantly in their behavior from rear-wheel drive cars. This circumstance should be taken into account during management. Keep in mind that when driving in a straight line, a front-wheel drive car is not prone to skidding at significantly higher speeds compared to a rear-wheel drive car. It handles the road well. But on turns, especially wet and icy ones, if you do not use the “cornering technique”, it can not only skid, but be carried away, and a simultaneous loss of traction of the wheels of both axles with the road occurs. This phenomenon usually ends in an accident. A case where the rear axle skids is not so bad. In such a situation, gradually increase the fuel supply. Rear wheel grip will increase. Use the steering wheel to adjust the direction of movement (“Driving techniques”).

questions.question: What information must be provided to the dispatcher to call an ambulance in case of an accident?

answers.text: Indicate well-known landmarks closest to the accident site. Report the number of victims, indicate their gender and age
Indicate the street and house number closest to the accident site. Report who was injured in the accident (pedestrian, car driver or passengers) and describe the injuries they received.

Indicate the location of the accident (name the street, house number and well-known landmarks closest to the accident site). Report: the number of victims, their gender, approximate age, whether they have consciousness, breathing, circulation, as well as severe bleeding, fractures and other injuries. Wait for a message from the dispatcher that the call has been accepted.

questions.comment: The most complete information allows the Emergency Medical Service to determine the number of teams of medical specialists to be sent, their specialization, simplifies the choice of route and reduces the arrival time of the Ambulance and other services.

questions.question: How many lanes does this road have?
questions.comment: A solid line of horizontal markings 1.1 is often used. It can be used to distribute traffic flows and to mark lane boundaries. In this case, it separates the traffic flows of one narrow roadway, on which, judging by the car, there is one lane in each direction, i.e. two. Motorcyclists move along one lane in two rows, which is not prohibited for them. (“Horizontal markings”, paragraphs 1.2, 9.1 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: These signs warn you:

answers.text: About the presence of dangerous turns after 500 m
The fact that at a distance of 150 - 300 m behind the road sign a 500 m long section of road with dangerous turns will begin
The fact that immediately after the sign a 500 m long section with dangerous turns will begin

questions.comment: Table 8.2.1 “Availability area” indicates the length of a number of dangerous turns, the first of which - to the left - begins after 150 - 300 m. ("Road signs" 8.2.1, 1.12.2)

questions.question: Which of the following signs applies only to the lane over which it is installed?
questions.comment: A sign with a sign 8.14 “Traffic Lane” (“A”) indicating the traffic lane covered by the sign or traffic light. (“Road Signs”)

questions.question: You are towing a disabled vehicle. In which lane can you continue driving in a populated area?
questions.comment: In the course of your movement, a sign 5.15.3 "The beginning of the lane" is installed. On the main lane, the sign 4.6 "Minimum speed limit" introduced a restriction – the minimum speed must be at least 60 km/h. The driver who cannot continue driving at the specified speed must change to the right lane. The towing mechanical vehicle is allowed to move at a speed of no more than 50 km/h. You should continue driving only in the right lane.("Traffic Signs", clause 10.4 of the Traffic Rules)

questions.question: What does the marking in the form of the inscription “STOP” on the roadway mean?

answers.text: Warns of approaching the stop line before an adjustable intersection
Warns of approaching the stop line and the "No stopping" sign
Warns of approaching the "Give way" sign

questions.comment: Marking 1.21 (inscription “STOP”) warns of approaching the stop line (marking 1.12) when it is used in combination with sign 2.5 “Moving without stopping is prohibited.” (“Horizontal marking”)

questions.question: Which vehicles are allowed to drive straight ahead?
questions.comment: The intersection is controlled. This roadway is controlled by lanes. The red signal of the far right traffic light prohibits movement from the far right lane. Driving straight from the middle lane is allowed. Driving left and turning around are allowed from the leftmost lane. With such traffic signals, only a truck is allowed to move straight ahead. (Clause 6.2 and paragraph 6.3 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: You intend to continue driving along the main road. Are you required to turn on the right turn indicators?

answers.text: Obligated only if there is a vehicle moving behind

questions.comment: Regardless of where you turn at an intersection, left or right on the main road, you should definitely turn on the appropriate turn signal. In this situation, turn on the right turn signal. The answer is “obligated.” (“Road signs”, paragraph 8.1 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Who should give way?
questions.comment: Sign 5.15.5 “End of lane” indicates the end of an uphill lane or acceleration lane. In any case, when changing lanes from it, you must give way to vehicles moving in the same direction without changing the direction of movement. (“Road signs”, clause 8.4 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: You can perform a reversal:

answers.text: Along any trajectory of the specified

questions.comment: If there are tram tracks on the left in the same direction, located at the same level as the roadway, to make a U-turn, you must drive onto the tram tracks in advance and then perform the maneuver. In this case, there should be no interference with the tram. You can only make a turn along trajectory “B”. (Clause 8.5, 9.6 of traffic rules)

questions.question: On which lane of the carriageway is traffic allowed in the locality, if for technical reasons the vehicle cannot reach a speed of more than 40 km/h?

answers.text: No further than the second lane
On any but the extreme left

questions.comment: Vehicles whose speed should not exceed 40 km/h or which, for technical reasons, cannot reach such a speed, must move in the far right lane, regardless of where and on what road the traffic is taking place. The exception is cases of detour, overtaking or changing lanes before a turn or U-turn. (Clause 9.5 of traffic rules)
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: Are you allowed to overtake a motorcycle?

answers.text: Allowed only after passing through an intersection

questions.comment: Overtaking is prohibited at uncontrolled intersections when driving on a road that is not the main one. The motorcyclist and you, according to sign 2.1 “Main Road”, are moving along the main road. Accordingly, you can overtake. (“Road signs”, paragraph 11.4 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Are you allowed to stop to pick up a passenger at this location?

answers.text: Permitted if it does not interfere with the movement of route vehicles

questions.comment: In places where route vehicles stop, stopping to pick up or disembark passengers is allowed, but this should not interfere with the movement of route vehicles. (Clause 12.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to drive through the intersection in the forward direction. What are your actions?

answers.text: Give way only to oncoming cars
Give way only to a car with a flashing light and a special sound signal on.

questions.comment: The intersection is adjustable. The first to pass will be an “operative” with special signals, who may deviate from the requirements of traffic light signals. Other drivers must ensure unhindered passage through the intersection. The truck driver is obliged to yield to you, i.e. to a vehicle moving straight from the oncoming direction. (Paragraphs 3.1, 3.2, 13.3, 13.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Who should you give way to when turning right?

answers.text: Only for a pedestrian crossing the roadway at an unregulated pedestrian crossing
Only for pedestrians crossing the roadway you are turning onto

questions.comment: Initially, you must give way to a pedestrian at an unregulated pedestrian crossing. (Clause 14.1 of the Traffic Regulations). Subsequently, when turning right, give way to pedestrians crossing the roadway you are turning onto. (Clause 13.1 of the Traffic Regulations). You should do the same with people using SIM cards to move around. This rule applies when driving through both controlled and uncontrolled intersections.
topic: Pedestrian crossings and stops of fixed-route vehicles

questions.question: What should you do when performing a U-turn?

answers.text: Give way only to passenger cars

questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. Vehicles on the main road have priority. When turning left and making a U-turn, you give way to vehicles moving directly from the opposite direction. In this situation, give way only to a passenger car. (Clause 13.9, 13.12 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Which of the following actions are prohibited for drivers of motor vehicles in a residential area?
questions.comment: Through traffic, practice driving, parking with the engine running in a residential area and in courtyard areas is prohibited. (Clause 17.2, 17.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: What distance must be provided between the towing and towed vehicles when towing with a rigid hitch?
questions.comment: When towing on a rigid hitch, the distance between the towing and towed vehicle should be no more than 4 m.(Clause 20.3 of the SDA)

questions.question: In what cases is it permissible to operate a vehicle?

answers.text: Optical elements not provided for by the design of the light device are installed
Headlight adjustment does not meet established requirements
Lenses of external lighting devices are missing or damaged
The front of the vehicle is equipped with orange-colored lights.

questions.comment: The third section “Lighting and light signaling devices” of the “List of faults” prohibits the operation of vehicles in cases where optical elements not provided for by the design of the light device are installed; headlight adjustment does not meet established requirements; the lenses of external lighting devices are missing or damaged (clauses 3.1, 3.2, 3.3). This list allows the operation of a vehicle on which lights with orange lights are installed at the front. (“List of faults”, paragraph 3.6)
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: What should a driver do to prevent the dangerous consequences of a car skidding when turning the steering wheel sharply on a slippery road?

answers.text: Quickly but smoothly turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid, then use a proactive influence on the steering wheel to align the trajectory of movement
Disengage the clutch and turn the steering wheel in the direction of skidding
Press the brake pedal and use the steering wheel to align the trajectory

questions.comment: To avoid having to deal with skidding on a slippery road, you should not brake sharply, change the direction of movement, or manipulate the gas pedal. You should choose a speed that ensures reliable traction between the wheels and the road. This is a basic precaution. In this “no panic” situation, perform actions only with the steering wheel.

questions.question: How should you place your hands on the victim's chest when performing cardiopulmonary resuscitation?

answers.text: The bases of the palms of both hands, taken in a “lock,” should be located on the chest two fingers above the xiphoid process so that the thumb of one hand points towards the victim’s left shoulder, and the other towards the right shoulder. The arms are straightened at the elbow joints.

The base of the palm of one hand is placed on the middle of the chest two fingers above the xiphoid process, the second hand is placed on top, the fingers are locked. The arms are straightened at the elbow joints, the thumbs pointing to the chin and stomach. Pressure should be carried out without sudden movements.

Hand pressure on the sternum is performed with the heel of the palm of one hand, located on the chest two fingers above the xiphoid process. The arm is straightened at the elbow joint. The direction of the thumb does not matter.

questions.comment: Please note that in the correct answer “the palms of both hands are placed on top of each other,” since performing chest compressions requires great physical effort. Order of the Ministry of Health and Social Development of Russia dated May 4, 2012 No. 477n, instead of the term “indirect cardiac massage,” the term “hand pressure on the victim’s sternum” was approved. The human heart is located in the middle of the chest - behind the sternum, 2 fingers above its xiphoid process (the triangular bone with which the sternum ends).

questions.question: How many carriageways does this road have?
questions.comment: This horizontal marking 1.3 does not divide the road into carriageways. Therefore, in the situation depicted, the road has four lanes and one carriageway. (Clause 1.2 of the traffic rules, the term “Dividing strip”)

questions.question: In the presence of which sign must a driver give way if oncoming traffic is difficult to pass?
questions.comment: On slopes marked with the signs: “A” - 1.13 “Steep descent” and “B” - 1.14 “Steep climb” - in the presence of an obstacle, the driver of a vehicle moving downhill must give way. On narrow sections of the road where oncoming traffic is difficult, signs are installed: on one side - “B” - 2.6 “Advantage to oncoming traffic”, on the other side - “G” - 2.7 “Advantage over oncoming traffic”. In this case, if oncoming traffic is difficult, it is prohibited to enter the narrow section of the road from sign 2.6. Answer - signs “A” and “B.” (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Are you allowed to park in the indicated location?
questions.comment: The effect of sign 3.27 “Stopping is prohibited” extends from the installation site to the nearest intersection, and in the absence of an intersection, to the end of the populated area. In this case, up to sign 5.24.1 “End of a populated area.” You have the right to stop on the side of the road behind the sign. (“Road Signs”)

questions.question: Did the truck driver violate the parking rules?

answers.text: Did not violate if the permissible maximum weight of the vehicle is not more than 3.5 tons

questions.comment: In a sidewalk parking lot marked with signs 6.4 “Parking (parking space)” and 8.6.4 “Method of parking a vehicle,” only a passenger car or motorcycle can be parked in this manner. Trucks, regardless of their permissible maximum weight (permitted maximum weight), are not allowed to park in this place. This driver violated the Rules. Don't confuse the table. 8.6.4 “Method of parking the vehicle” from table. 8.4.3 “Type of vehicle”, otherwise make a mistake. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: What does the vertical marking on the road fence warn you about?

answers.text: About driving on a dangerous section of the road

questions.comment: Vertical markings 2.5 indicate the side surfaces of road fences on small radius curves, steep slopes, and other dangerous areas.

questions.question: Is the driver allowed to continue driving after the green light changes to yellow, if it is possible to stop before the intersection only by applying emergency braking?

answers.text: Permitted if the driver intends to drive through the intersection only in the forward direction

questions.comment: Emergency (as sharp as possible) braking is used only to prevent a traffic accident (RTA). Therefore, the rules allow driving under a yellow traffic light if stopping would require you to brake urgently. (Clause 6.2, 6.14, 10.5 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: The hand of the motorcycle rider raised up is a signal informing you of his intention:

answers.text: Slow down to stop and give way to cars

questions.comment: The intersection is equal. The motorcyclist has an obstacle on the right. He is obliged to give way, i.e. slow down and stop. This is indicated by his outstretched hand. (Clause 8.1, 13.11 of the Traffic Rules)

questions.question: In which directions can you continue driving in the left lane in a truck with a permissible maximum weight of no more than 3.5 tons?
questions.comment: The effect of the sign according to plate 8.4.1 “Type of vehicle” applies to trucks, including those with a trailer, with a permissible maximum weight of more than 3.5 tons. The effect of the sign does not apply to you, therefore, from the occupied lane you can continue driving straight, to the left, make a U-turn, to move in the opposite direction. (“Road Signs”, paragraph 8.5 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You need to turn onto the road adjacent to the right. What are your actions?

answers.text: Without changing lanes, reduce speed, then change lanes
Without changing speed, change lanes, then reduce speed

questions.comment: You should reduce speed only in the deceleration lane. (Clause 8.10 of traffic rules)

questions.question: At what maximum speed do you have the right to continue driving a car with a trailer outside a populated area?
questions.comment: Outside a populated area, on roads other than highways, a passenger car with a trailer is allowed to drive at a speed of no more than 70 km/h (Clause 10.3 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: Are you allowed to overtake?

answers.text: Allowed if overtaking is completed before the intersection

questions.comment: Overtaking is prohibited at equivalent intersections. You, according to sign 2.3.1 “Intersection with a secondary road,” are moving in the direction of the main road. You can overtake. (“Road signs”, paragraph 11.4 of traffic regulations)

questions.question: Which driver violated the parking rules?

answers.text: Only the driver of car A
Only the driver of car B

questions.comment: Vehicles are allowed to be parked in one row parallel to the edge of the roadway. This rule also applies to local widening of the roadway (as in this situation). The exception is such places that have a combination of sign 6.4 with one of the plates 8.6.1-8.6.9 The driver of car “A” violates the parking rules. (Clause 12.2 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to turn around. What are your actions?

answers.text: Make a U-turn to give way to a car
Wait until the traffic controller lowers his right hand

questions.comment: The intersection is controlled. The traffic controller's right arm is extended forward. From the left side, vehicles can continue moving in any direction, observing the rules for the location of vehicles on the roadway. When making a U-turn from the leftmost lane, you will have an obstacle on the right. You will give way to a car turning right. (Clause 6.10, 13.4 of traffic rules)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: Who should you give way to when driving in a straight direction?
questions.comment: The intersection is equal. In equal conditions, the tram has an advantage, and trackless vehicles are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves, i.e. whoever has an obstacle on the right gives way. In this situation, you only give way to the tram. (Clause 13.11 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: What should you do when turning left?

answers.text: Give way only to a truck with a flashing light on

questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. The yellow flashing light on the truck does not give him an advantage. Vehicles located on the main road have priority. You pass first, followed by cars on the secondary road, which are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves. A passenger car will pass second, a truck will pass last. (Clause 3.4, 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Are you allowed to cross a railway crossing?

answers.text: Allowed, since the crossing officer prohibits the movement of only the oncoming car
Allowed if there is no approaching train

questions.comment: The prohibitory signal of the crossing duty officer is when he addresses drivers with a baton, a red lantern or flag raised above his head, or with his arms extended to the side. At the same time, traveling to the crossing from both the chest and the back is prohibited (remember the aphorism “chest, back is a wall”) (Clause 15.3 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: In what cases is it permissible to use sound signals in populated areas?

answers.text: Only for warning of intent to overtake
Only to prevent a traffic accident
In both of the above cases

questions.comment: Sound signals can only be used: – to warn other drivers of the intention to overtake outside populated areas; – in cases where it is necessary to prevent a traffic accident. (Clause 19.10 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Use of external lighting fixtures and audible signals

questions.question: At what maximum value of the total play in the steering is a passenger car allowed to be used?
questions.comment: The total play in the steering of a passenger car should not exceed 10 degrees. (“List of faults” paragraph 2.3)
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: What should a driver do when getting out of a car parked at the sidewalk or on the side of the road?

answers.text: Walk around the front of the car
Walk around the car from behind

questions.comment: The rules do not regulate the driver's actions when disembarking from the car. But given the conditions of road safety in such situations, in most cases, you should go around the car from behind in order to be able to see vehicles moving in the same direction. The main condition for safety when leaving the car in such situations is that the actions of the driver and other persons should not be a surprise for other drivers.

questions.question: When driving in foggy conditions, the distance to objects appears:
questions.comment: When driving in foggy conditions, the distance to objects appears greater than in reality. This is explained by a psychological factor. A person compares everything with familiar, ordinary conditions in which he spends most of his time, i.e. with daytime conditions.

questions.question: What is the permissible maximum weight of a vehicle?

answers.text: The maximum permissible weight of cargo for transportation, established by the manufacturer
Weight of the equipped vehicle excluding the weight of the driver, passengers and cargo, established by the manufacturer
The mass of the equipped vehicle with cargo, driver and passengers, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permissible

questions.comment: Paragraph 1.2 of the traffic rules is the term “Permitted maximum weight”.

questions.question: Are you allowed to continue driving?
questions.comment: Sign 3.18.2 “No left turn” does not prohibit making a U-turn. Therefore, you can, at your discretion, continue driving straight or turn around and continue driving in the opposite direction. (“Road Signs”)

questions.question: Which of the following signs permit travel by car to your place of residence or work?
questions.comment: The following signs allow travel by car to the place of residence or work: “A” - 3.2 “Movement prohibited”, “B” - 3.3 “Movement of motor vehicles is prohibited”. Of the prohibition signs, 6 signs provide such a “benefit”. These do not include sign “B” - 3.1 “Entry prohibited”, which prohibits entry under the sign of all vehicles, except for route vehicles and vehicles, in the case of using sign 3.1 with plates 8.4.1 - 8.4.8; 8.5.1, 8.5.2, 8.5.3, 8.5.4, 8.5.5 - 8.5.7 and 8.4.9 - 8.4.16. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: What do these road signs mean?

answers.text: Parking space for buses and trolleybuses
Parking space where it is possible to transfer to a fixed-route vehicle (bus or trolleybus)

questions.comment: Sign 6.4 “Parking (parking space)” is used with plate 8.21.2 “Type of route vehicle.” This combination of signs shows that from this place for further movement you can use route vehicles - a bus or a trolleybus, and you can leave your car in an equipped parking lot. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Triangle lane markings:

answers.text: Indicates a dangerous section of the road
Warns you about approaching a place where you need to give way
Indicates the place where you need to stop

questions.comment: Marking 1.20 warns of approaching marking 1.13, which indicates the place where the driver must, if necessary, stop to give way to vehicles moving along the road being crossed. (“Horizontal markings”)

questions.question: Is it permissible to continue driving if the traffic controller raised his hand up after you entered the intersection?
questions.comment: You are at a crossroads. You should release it, otherwise you will interfere with the movement of vehicles moving from other directions. (Clause 6.14 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: You intend to continue driving along the main road. Are you required to turn on your left turn signals?

answers.text: Obligated if vehicles are approaching from other directions

questions.comment: Wherever you drive, you must strictly adhere to “your internal rule,” which can be formulated as follows: “My driving is safe when my actions are clear to all other road users.” You intend to make a left turn - be sure to inform other road users about this by turning on the turn signal. (Clause 8.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Who must give way when changing lanes?

answers.text: Drivers should act by mutual agreement

questions.comment: When changing lanes at the same time, drivers are guided by the “right-hand rule.” The truck driver has an obstacle on his right. He gives way. (Clause 8.4 of traffic rules)

questions.question: In what directions can you continue moving?
questions.comment: On your side there is a broken marking line 1.11, which allows its intersection. Since you are on the far left lane, you can continue driving straight, turn left, or turn around and continue driving in the opposite direction. (“Horizontal markings”, clause 8.5 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: At what maximum speed do you have the right to continue driving a car?
questions.comment: Higher speeds are allowed on the motorway. In this case, the permissible maximum speed is 110 km/h. (“Road signs” 5.1. “Highway”, clause 10.3 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: What should you do in this situation?

answers.text: Give way to an oncoming car
Act by mutual agreement with the driver of the oncoming car

questions.comment: There is an obstacle on your side of the roadway - an obstacle in the form of a broken down car. You must give way. If a similar situation had developed on a slope indicated by signs 1.13 “Steep descent”, 1.14 “Steep climb”, then the car moving downhill would have to give way, i.e. down. (Clause 11.7 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Are you allowed to park your car in this place?

answers.text: Permitted if it does not interfere with the movement of route vehicles

questions.comment: Stopping and parking are prohibited closer than 15 m from the stopping places of route vehicles (the condition is not violated), as well as at a pedestrian crossing and closer than 5 m to it. By stopping close to a pedestrian crossing, you will violate this requirement. Therefore, parking a vehicle in this place is prohibited. (Clause 12.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to turn left. What are your actions?

answers.text: Give way to the tram when turning off the roadway
Let the tram pass, change lanes onto the tram tracks in the same direction and make a turn from them

questions.comment: A traffic light with white and moon colored signals, intended for drivers of route vehicles, allows them to move straight. According to the green traffic light, you are also allowed to move in any direction. To turn left, you must let the tram pass, change lanes onto the tram tracks in the same direction and turn left from them. (Clause 6.2, 6.8, 8.5).
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: Who do you have to give way to when turning left?
questions.comment: At intersections, whether regulated or not, when turning left or right, the driver is obliged to give way to pedestrians crossing the roadway into which he is turning. You should also give way to a cyclist moving straight towards you. (Clause 13.1, 13.2 of traffic rules)

questions.question: In what case will you have to give way to a traffic police vehicle?

answers.text: If the traffic police vehicle has blue flashing lights on
If the traffic police vehicle has blue flashing lights and a special sound signal on at the same time

questions.comment: In this case, you must give way to the “operative” if the blue flashing lights and a special sound signal are turned on at the same time on this vehicle. (Clause 3.2 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: When approaching a stopped vehicle with the hazard lights on, which has the “Transportation of Children” markings, the driver must:

answers.text: If necessary, stop and let children pass
Carry out all the above actions

questions.comment: The hazard warning lights must be turned on when children are boarding or disembarking from a bus that has the “Transportation of Children” identification signs. When approaching a stopped bus with the hazard lights on and bearing the “Transportation of Children” identification signs, the driver must slow down, if necessary, stop and let the children pass, i.e. carry out all of the above actions. It must be taken into account that from March 1, 2023, organized transportation of children is permitted only on buses. (Clause 7.1, 14.7, 22.6 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Pedestrian crossings and stops of fixed-route vehicles

questions.question: In what cases do moped drivers violate the Rules?

answers.text: Only if they drive a moped without holding the handlebars with at least one hand
Only if they move on the road without a fastened motorcycle helmet
In both of the above cases

questions.comment: Moped drivers are prohibited from: – driving a moped without holding the steering wheel with at least one hand; – moving on the road without a fastened motorcycle helmet. The correct answer is in both of these cases. (Clause 24.8 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Training riding and additional requirements for the movement of cyclists

questions.question: Operation of the vehicle is prohibited if there is a transparent colored film at the top of the windshield with a width of more than:
questions.comment: Paragraph 4.3 of the “List of Faults” prohibits the operation of the vehicle if there is a transparent color film more than 140 mm wide in the upper part of the windshield.
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: If you stop on an uphill (downhill) slope and there is a shoulder, you can prevent the car from spontaneously rolling onto the roadway by turning its front wheels to the position:
questions.comment: Wheels turned towards the ditch (“A” and “D”), in the event of an unintentional rolling of the car, will lead the uncontrolled vehicle into the ditch, which will avoid oncoming collisions with moving vehicles. And vice versa.

questions.question: The established fact of the driver's use of substances that cause alcohol intoxication is determined by the presence in his body of absolute ethyl alcohol in a concentration exceeding:

answers.text: 0.10 milligrams per liter of exhaled air
0.16 milligrams per liter of exhaled air
0.25 milligrams per liter of exhaled air

questions.comment: Article 12.8 of the Code of Administrative Offenses, which provides for the punishment of drivers who are intoxicated, stipulates that it comes into force if the presence of absolute ethyl alcohol in a concentration exceeds 0.16 milligrams per liter of exhaled air.

questions.question: Can the owner of a motorcycle with a displacement of an internal combustion engine not exceeding 125 cm3 and a maximum power not exceeding 11 kW transfer control of this vehicle in his presence to another person, having an insurance policy of compulsory civil liability insurance on paper or in the form of an electronic document or a copy thereof on paper?

answers.text: Maybe if this person has a driver’s license for the right to drive a vehicle of category “A” or subcategory “A1”
Maybe if this person has a driver’s license to drive a vehicle of subcategory “B1”
Maybe if this person has a driver’s license to drive a vehicle of category “M”
Maybe in all of the above cases

questions.comment: Article 25, paragraph 7 of the Federal Law “On Road Safety” does not prohibit the transfer of control of a vehicle to another person who has a driver’s identity card of this category or subcategory and the corresponding insurance policy or information printed on paper about the conclusion of the corresponding compulsory insurance agreement in the form of an electronic document. In this case, to drive a motorcycle you must have a category A or subcategory A1 license.

questions.question: What do these road signs inform you about?

answers.text: About approaching an intersection where there is a “Give Way” sign
About approaching an intersection where there is a sign “Driving without stopping is prohibited”

questions.comment: Table 8.1.2 “Distance to object” indicates the distance from sign 2.4 “Give way” to the intersection if immediately before the intersection there is sign 2.5 “Driving without stopping is prohibited.” (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Are you allowed to stay at the indicated place?

answers.text: Allowed only for boarding and disembarking passengers

questions.comment: The solid yellow marking line 1.4 indicates places where stopping is prohibited. From March 1, 2023, this marking can be used independently. It is excluded from the definition of the coverage area of ​​sign 3.27 “Stopping is prohibited”. In this situation it is functionally ineffective. Stopping in the indicated place is PROHIBITED. (“Road signs”, “Horizontal markings”).

questions.question: Which of the following signs only applies to the nearest intersection in the direction of travel?
questions.comment: The effect of the signs: B – 3.24 “Maximum speed limit” and D – 3.28 “Parking prohibited” extends to the nearest intersection beyond it, and in populated areas, in the absence of an intersection, to the end of the populated area. The effect of the signs: A – 5.31 “Zone with maximum speed limitation” and B – 5.27 “Zone with limited parking” is canceled by the corresponding signs 5.32 “End of zone with maximum speed limitation” and 5.28 “End of zone with limited parking.” (“Road signs”)

questions.question: What do the broken lines at an intersection mean?

answers.text: Mandatory direction of movement at an intersection
Warning about approaching the markings separating traffic flows of opposite or associated directions

questions.comment: “Horizontal markings” 1.7 indicate traffic lanes within the intersection.

questions.question: You are allowed to move:
questions.comment: If there is a traffic controller, traffic light signals “do not work.” From the left side, with the traffic controller’s right arm extended, trackless vehicles are allowed to move in all directions. But, because You are in the right lane, you are only allowed to move straight or to the right. (Clause 6.10 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: When should you turn off your left turn signals when overtaking?

answers.text: Immediately after changing lanes into oncoming traffic
After overtaking the vehicle being overtaken
At the discretion of the driver

questions.comment: You have completed changing lanes into the oncoming lane, stop signaling immediately. If you are ahead of a vehicle in the oncoming lane, do not give a signal. (Clause 8.2 of the traffic rules. “Driving techniques.” Overtaking)

questions.question: Is a passenger car driver required to give way to a truck driver?

answers.text: Obligated if the truck driver begins to move to the right

questions.comment: The driver of a passenger car is the “owner” of the lane, and therefore is not obliged to yield. (Clause 8.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Are you allowed to make a U-turn on this section of the road?

answers.text: Permitted only when road visibility is at least 100 m

questions.comment: In the course of your movement, the road turns to the right. U-turn is allowed only when the road is visible for more than 100 m.(Clause 8.11 of the SDA)

questions.question: At what speed are motorcycles allowed to travel outside built-up areas on motorways?
questions.comment: Outside populated areas, motorcycles are allowed to travel on highways at a speed of no more than 110 km/h (Clause 10.3 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Are you allowed to change lanes to the middle lane at the end of the climb to get ahead of the truck?

answers.text: Permitted only when road visibility is at least 100 m

questions.comment: In this situation, there is a clear demarcation of the road into lanes. One lane with oncoming traffic and two lanes in your direction. Therefore, you can advance at the end of the climb. But always exercise caution in such situations, because what is happening on the road behind the transverse fracture is not visible, it is unknown. Do not get into situations in which an instant surprise occurs. (Traffic rules: 1.2 term “Advanced”, 11.4)

questions.question: In which of the following places can you park your car?
questions.comment: The action takes place in a populated area on a section of road marked with sign 5.5 “One-way road.” On such a road, stopping and parking is allowed on the left side of the road in the direction of travel (at place “A”). Place “B” is located within the coverage area of ​​sign 3.28 “Parking prohibited.” Therefore, at your discretion, you can park the car in place “A” or “B”. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: What should you do when turning left?

answers.text: Drive beyond the stop line and stop at the intersection to give way to an oncoming car
Stop in front of the stop line and turn left after a passenger car has passed.

questions.comment: Stopping no further than the stop line is required when there is a prohibiting traffic light signal. The green light is on for you. Without stopping, drive to the intersection and, before turning left, stop to give way to a passenger car moving straight from the opposite direction. (“Horizontal markings,” paragraphs 6.13, 6.2, 13.3, 13.4 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Are you allowed to enter an intersection beyond which there is a traffic jam?

answers.text: Allowed if you intend to make a turn

questions.comment: In this situation, you can only enter the intersection to turn, since the resulting traffic jam makes it impossible to move in the forward direction without a forced stop at the intersection, and this will create an obstacle to movement in the transverse direction (Clause 13.2 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: You intend to continue straight ahead. Who do you have to give way to?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles on the main road have priority and are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves. After they have passed, using the same rule, vehicles on the secondary road pass. You pass first, without yielding to anyone, the motorcyclist is second, the truck is third, the passenger car is last. (“Road signs”, clauses 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Where can pedestrians move in a residential area?

answers.text: Along the sidewalks and in one row along the edge of the carriageway
On sidewalks and along the entire width of the roadway

(Clause 23.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: In what cases is it permitted to operate a vehicle?

The exhaust noise level exceeds the established standards

Be especially attentive to fuel leakage, which can be caused by an odor. Such a malfunction threatens to cause the car to catch fire, which cannot always be extinguished. Operation is not prohibited if the coolant temperature indicator does not work. (“List of faults”)
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: When driving through deep snow on a dirt road, you should:

In a pre-selected low gear, without sharp turns or stops
In a pre-selected high gear, without sharp turns or stops

questions.question: What is the optimal position for a conscious victim if a spinal injury is suspected?

Lay the victim on his back on a hard, flat surface, do not move him unless necessary, do not change his position
Lay the victim on his back, place a cushion of clothing under his neck and elevate his legs

questions.question: What actions should the drivers involved immediately take in the event of a traffic accident?

Report the incident to the police

questions.question: The driver of a passenger car must turn off the left turn indicators:

After being ahead of the truck
After returning to the right lane

questions.question: Did the truck driver violate the parking rules?

questions.comment: You cannot park your car on the roadway, since the distance between the car and the solid marking line will be less than 3 m, which is unacceptable. Trucks of any type are not permitted to park either partially or fully on the sidewalk. This is only allowed for drivers of cars and motorcycles, and only in places marked with appropriate signs. questions.question: Which driver making a turn will violate the Rules?
questions.comment: Sign 4.1.1 “Move straight” in this case is installed immediately before the intersection of roadways, i.e. before the intersection. You can only continue moving straight ahead. In this situation, both drivers violate the Rules. (“Road Signs”)

questions.question: You intend to continue moving in a forward direction. What are your actions?

answers.text: Give way to cars and motorcycles

questions.comment: The intersection is equal. When determining the order in which vehicles travel through an intersection, we are guided by the “right-hand rule,” i.e. Whoever has an obstacle on the right concedes. The peculiarity of solving this issue is to roll out and stop at the intersection of a vehicle starting to move. The driver of the car starts moving first, turning left, since at the initial moment there is no obstacle on the right. Having reached the middle of the intersection, before turning left, he will stop, as he must give way to the motorcyclist on his right. After this, there will be no obstacle on the right on the trajectory of your car - you pass the intersection first. The motorcyclist is after you. And the last one to finish crossing the intersection is the driver who started moving. (Clause 13.11 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Who should you give way to when turning left?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles on the main road have priority. Between themselves, trackless vehicles are guided by the “right-hand rule”, giving way to a tram, which, under equal conditions, has an advantage over them. Tram “B” passes first, then a passenger car, and you after them. Tram “A” will pass last, since it is located on a secondary road. (Clause 13.9, 13.1, 13.11 Traffic Regulations)

Only in special parking areas marked with appropriate signs

questions.question: How to provide first aid for frostbite and hypothermia?

answers.text: Rub the affected areas of the body with snow or wool, then insulate them, give them alcohol, and move them to a warm room
Insulate the affected areas of the body and immobilize them, wrap the victim in warm clothes or a blanket, give a warm drink, move to a warm room
Lubricate the affected areas of the body with cream, apply a warm compress and a heating pad, move to a warm room, give a warm drink

questions.comment: It is PROHIBITED to give alcohol in the cold; it dilates the blood vessels of the skin, increasing the release of heat by the body. In case of frostbite and hypothermia, it is necessary to minimize heat loss from the surface of the victim’s body. To do this, they insulate the affected areas of the body and immobilize them, wrap the victim in warm clothes or a blanket, give him a warm drink, and move him to a warm room.

For the right to drive a vehicle of category “B”
