questions.question: Who has the advantage in movement?
questions.comment: The driver of a car enters the road from the adjacent territory (from a gas station). He is obliged to give way to vehicles moving along the road being crossed; accordingly, the truck driver has “advantage.” (Clause 1.2, 8.3 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Is the driver allowed to reverse to pick up a passenger on this section of the road?

answers.text: Allowed if the driver is driving a passenger taxi

questions.comment: Sign 4.1.1 “Move straight” does not prohibit reversing if it occurs outside the boundaries of the intersection. In this section, you can drive up to the passenger in reverse, subject to the conditions stated above. (“Road signs”, paragraph 8.12 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Are you allowed, while driving a truck with a permissible maximum weight of more than 2.5 tons, to enter the third lane in this situation?

answers.text: Permitted only for left turns or U-turns

questions.comment: The driver of a truck with a permissible maximum weight of more than 2.5 tons can drive into the leftmost lane if there are three or more lanes in a given direction only to turn left and make a U-turn. (Clause 9.4 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: Is it possible for you to overtake a tractor while driving a truck with a permissible maximum weight of no more than 3.5 tons?

answers.text: It is possible if the tractor speed is less than 30 km/h

questions.comment: Sign 3.22 “Overtaking by trucks is prohibited” does not apply to trucks with a permissible maximum weight of up to 3.5 tons. If you drive such a car, you can overtake. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: In what place and direction are you allowed to stop?
questions.comment: On a road that has one lane in each direction and does not have tram tracks in the middle, in a populated area marked with signs 5.23.1 and 5.23.2 “Beginning of a populated area” (with a white background), stopping and parking is allowed not only on the right side, but also on the left side of the road. Therefore, you are allowed to stop at any of the indicated places. (“Road signs”, clause 12.1 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Who do you have to give way to when turning left?
questions.comment: The intersection is adjustable. The tram in equivalent conditions has an advantage over trackless vehicles. Along with it, at the same time, since the trajectories do not intersect, a passenger car will pass, turning to the right, to which you must also give way when turning to the left. You will be the last to cross the intersection.(Clauses 13.3, 13.4, 13.6 of the Traffic Rules)

questions.question: You must give way to a truck:

answers.text: In both of the above cases

questions.comment: The intersection is equal. Drivers are guided by the “right hand rule”. You will have an obstacle on the right only when driving straight - you are giving way to a truck. When turning right, there is no obstacle on the right. (Clause 13.11 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to turn around. Who do you need to give way to?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles located on the main road have priority over others, regardless of their further direction of travel. They are guided by the “right hand rule” among themselves. The truck passes first, you pass after it, the passenger car passes last. (Clause 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 Traffic Rules)

questions.question: Where are you allowed to stop when driving on the motorway?

answers.text: Any place to the right of the line marking the edge of the roadway
Any place at the edge of the roadway

questions.comment: On the highway, it is prohibited to stop outside special parking areas marked with signs 6.4 “Parking (parking space)” or 7.11 “Rest place” (shown in the figure). At the same time, the distance to the designated place is 500 m. (“Road signs”, clause 16.1 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: While driving in the dark outside a populated area with your high beam headlights on, you caught up with a vehicle moving ahead. What are your actions?

answers.text: Leave the side lights on and turn off the high beams
Switch the high beam headlights to low beam

questions.comment: To eliminate the possibility of dazzling the overtaken driver through the rear-view mirrors, it is necessary to switch the high beam to the low beam. (Clause 19.2 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Use of external lighting fixtures and audible signals

questions.question: What should a driver do if the windshield washer fails while driving?

answers.text: Continue your intended trip with extreme caution
Attempt to rectify the fault on site, and if this is not possible, then proceed to the place of parking or repair with the necessary precautions

questions.comment: Clause 3 of the “Basic Provisions” prohibits the operation of a vehicle with malfunctions in the part related to road safety. Clause 2.3.1 of the Traffic Regulations does not prohibit further movement with such a malfunction to the parking or repair site in compliance with safety precautions.
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: What should you do if the rear axle of a rear-wheel drive car skids while turning?

answers.text: Increase the fuel supply, stabilize the movement with the steering wheel
Slow down and turn the steering wheel in the direction of skidding
Significantly reduce fuel delivery without changing the steering wheel position
Slightly reduce the fuel supply and turn the steering wheel in the direction of skidding

questions.comment: Don't get lost in such a situation. Don't let off the gas suddenly. Reduce engine speed as smoothly as possible; To level out the skid, turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: In what case does the driver need to assess the situation behind him?

answers.text: Before performing a maneuver (changing lanes or changing direction)
In all of the above cases

questions.comment: Before performing any maneuver, you should assess the situation behind you. In the above cases too. Typically this is done through the rear view mirrors. Keep in mind that they have “dead” (unvisible) zones. Therefore, it is advisable to avoid sudden maneuvers.

questions.question: What does it mean to give way?

answers.text: You must stop only if there is a "Give Way" sign.
You must stop to let other road users pass
You must not start, resume or continue driving, or perform any maneuver if this may force other road users who have priority over you to change direction or speed.

questions.comment: If you do not comply with the requirement to give way, then you are not just violating the Rules, but creating an emergency situation. (Clause 1.2, the term “Give way”)

questions.question: Which of the following signs provide the right of way at uncontrolled intersections?
questions.comment: Signs: 2.1 “Main Road” (“A”) and 2.3.5 “Adjunction of a Secondary Road” (“B”) provide the right of way at uncontrolled intersections to vehicles located on the main road. (Clause 1.2 term “Main Road”, 13.9 Traffic Rules)

questions.question: Are you allowed to overtake?

answers.text: Allowed if the motorcycle speed is no more than 30 km/h

questions.comment: We remember that sign 3.20 “Overtaking is prohibited” prohibits overtaking of all vehicles except low-speed vehicles, horse-drawn vehicles, mopeds and two-wheeled motorcycles without a side trailer. You are allowed to overtake, regardless of the speed of the motorcyclist. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Is it possible for the driver to park the truck in this location using the specified method?

answers.text: It is possible if the permissible maximum weight of the vehicle is not more than 3.5 tons

questions.comment: Truck drivers who have sign 6.4 “Parking (parking space)” with one of the signs 8.6.2, 8.6.3 and 8.6.6 - 8.6.9 “Method of parking vehicles” cannot stand in the area covered by this sign. It is not allowed for any trucks to park on the edge of the sidewalk and clause 12.2 of the traffic rules and in other places not marked with signs. Therefore, the answer is clear - the truck driver is violating the Rules. (“Road Signs”)

questions.question: This vertical marking indicates:

answers.text: Only the lower edge of the span of tunnels, bridges and overpasses
Any elements of road structures that pose a danger

questions.comment: Vertical markings 2.2 indicate the lower edge of the superstructure of tunnels, bridges and overpasses. (“Vertical markings”)

questions.question: Where should you stay?
questions.comment: If there is a stop line (marking 1.12) at a prohibitory traffic light signal, you should stop in front of the stop line. (“Horizontal markings”, clause 6.13 of the traffic rules)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: Should drivers use their turn signals when maneuvering in a parking lot or gas station?

answers.text: Should only be used if there are other vehicles in the immediate vicinity.

questions.comment: Always inform other road users of your intentions. It doesn’t matter where, under what conditions, under what circumstances you are a driver. Before starting maneuvering, you should turn on the appropriate turn signal. (Clause 8.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Which driver violates the rules of turning at an intersection?

answers.text: Only the driver of a motorcycle turning left

questions.comment: Both drivers violate the maneuvering rules when making a turn. Before turning, the motorcyclist had to take the extreme appropriate position on the roadway. When turning right, the driver of the car should move as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway. There is such an opportunity, he should have made a turn into the far right lane. (Clause 8.5, 8.6 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Is the driver allowed to reverse when there are no other road users?

answers.text: Allowed only up to the pedestrian crossing

questions.comment: Reversing on sections of roads marked with sign 5.5 “One-way road” is not prohibited. Therefore, you can perform the maneuver before the pedestrian crossing, since reversing is prohibited on them. (“Road signs”, paragraph 8.12 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Is it possible for you to enter the leftmost lane in this situation?

answers.text: It is possible if the horse-drawn cart moves at a speed of no more than 30 km/h

questions.comment: It is prohibited to enter the leftmost lane intended for oncoming traffic on a two-way road with three lanes. (Clause 9.3 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: Are you allowed to overtake?

answers.text: It is allowed if it does not interfere with other traffic participants.

questions.comment: The intersection is equal. Overtaking is prohibited at equivalent intersections. (Clause 11.4 of traffic regulations)

questions.question: Which driver violated the stopping rules?

answers.text: Only the driver of car A
Only the driver of car B

questions.comment: Don't confuse stopping with parking. Stopping is prohibited directly at a railway crossing, the boundaries of which are barriers. Parking is prohibited directly at the railway crossing and closer than 50 m from it. Drivers stopped outside the railway crossing without violating the rules. (Clause 12.4, 12.1 of traffic rules)

questions.question: When performing what maneuver does the driver of a car have the right of way?

answers.text: When performing any of the listed maneuvers

questions.comment: The driver of a passenger car, moving under the green arrow in the additional section, turned on simultaneously with the main green signal, can turn left and make a U-turn. At the same time, buses and trucks moving under the switched on green arrow, in an additional section that is switched on simultaneously with the main red signal, must yield to all other vehicles moving from all other directions. The driver of a passenger car has an advantage in this situation when performing any of the listed maneuvers. (Clause 13.5 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to turn left. What are your actions?

answers.text: Give way to the tram by turning from the left lane
Let the tram pass, change lanes onto tram tracks in the same direction, and then make a turn

questions.comment: You and the tram are in equal conditions. In this case, the tram has an advantage over trackless vehicles. Give way to the tram. (Clause 13.11 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: To whom do you have to give way when driving in a forward direction?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles located on the main road have priority. Between themselves they are guided by the “right hand rule”, i.e. whoever has an obstacle on the right concedes. You are on a secondary road - you give way to both vehicles. (“Road signs” 2.4, 8.13, clauses 13.9, 13.10 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Is it possible for you, while driving a truck, to get ahead in this situation?

answers.text: It is possible if the permissible maximum weight of the vehicle is no more than 2.5 tons

questions.comment: On any roads that have three or more lanes for traffic in a given direction, the leftmost lane is allowed to occupy only during heavy traffic, when other lanes are occupied, as well as for turning left or making a U-turn, and trucks with r.m.m. more than 2.5 tons - only for turning left or making a U-turn. You can advance if the r.m.m. truck no more than 2.5 tons (Clause 9.4 of traffic rules)

questions.question: When driving during daylight hours, the vehicle must have the following on:
questions.comment: During daylight hours, all moving vehicles, except bicycles, must have low beam headlights or daytime running lights turned on for the purpose of identifying them. Instead of low beam for this purpose, it is allowed to use fog lights. (Clause 19.4, 19.5 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Use of external lighting fixtures and audible signals

questions.question: It is prohibited to operate a passenger car (category M1) if the remaining tire tread depth (in the absence of wear indicators) is no more than:
questions.comment: It is prohibited to operate passenger cars (including category M1) with tires (in the absence of a wear indicator) with a remaining tread height of no more than 1.6 mm. (“List of faults” clause 5.4)
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: What should be done to quickly restore the effectiveness of a vehicle's brakes after driving through a water obstacle?

answers.text: Press the brake pedal sharply and then continue driving.
Continue driving and dry the brake pads by repeatedly pressing the brake pedal briefly.
Continue driving at low speed without braking

questions.comment: Some drivers do not attach importance to carrying out such an operation, which leads to collisions with obstacles, etc., since the effectiveness of “raw brakes” is sharply reduced, especially if the brake mechanisms are of the drum type. Dry the brakes by briefly pressing the brakes, after shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: What are the initial steps to take when providing first aid in the event of an injury resulting from a road accident?

answers.text: Wash the wound with water, remove foreign bodies embedded in the wound, apply sterile cotton wool, securing it with a bandage.
Put on medical gloves, wash the wound with an alcohol solution of iodine, lubricate it with medicinal ointment and seal it with a continuous adhesive plaster
Wear medical gloves, do not wash the wound, apply a sterile gauze napkin to the wound, securing it with an adhesive plaster around the edges or a bandage.

questions.comment: To avoid infection with infections transmitted from the victim through blood, when providing first aid, it is initially necessary to wear medical gloves, do not wash the wound, apply a sterile gauze cloth to it, securing it with an adhesive plaster around the edges or a bandage. It is impossible to seal the wound with a continuous adhesive plaster (seal it), as this will lead to subsequent complications.

questions.question: Which picture shows an intersection?
questions.comment: An intersection is a place where roads cross, join or branch at the same level. The left picture shows an unequal intersection. Exits from adjacent territories are not considered intersections. Example - right picture. (Clause 1.2 of traffic rules)

questions.question: You can perform a reversal:

answers.text: Along any trajectory of the specified

questions.comment: The effect of the sign 4.1.1 “Go straight”, if installed before the intersection of roadways, applies only to the first intersection behind the sign. You can make a U-turn along trajectory “B”. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Are you allowed to park your car in this place on odd days of the month?
questions.comment: The action takes place in a populated area, on a road with one lane in each direction, without tram tracks in the middle. On such a road you can stop and park not only on the right side of the road, but also on the left, if there are no prohibiting signs. In this situation, the following signs were used simultaneously: on the right side 3.29 “Parking is prohibited on odd days of the month”, on the left side 3.30 “Parking is prohibited on even days of the month.” When parking a car in this case, please note that from 21.00 to 24.00 these signs are not valid due to the rearrangement of vehicles. Therefore, the car can be parked at the intended location from 21.00 on an odd day to 24.00 on an even number. Allowed only after 21.00. (“Road signs”, paragraph 12.1 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Which of the following signs indicate areas where the driver is required to give way to pedestrians on the roadway?
questions.comment: Signs: “B” - 5.19.2 “Pedestrian crossing”, “B” - 5.21 “Residential zone” give priority to pedestrians on the roadway on sections of roads and territories designated by them. Warning sign “A” - 1.22 “Pedestrian crossing” warns of approaching a pedestrian crossing marked with signs 5.19.1, 5.19.2 and (or) markings 1.14.1 and 1.14.2. Installed in N.P. beyond 50-100 m, outside N.P. for 150-300 m. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: What does the A100 marking on the road mean?

answers.text: Distance to the nearest populated area

questions.comment: This horizontal marking 1.22 indicates the road number.

questions.question: You can continue moving:
questions.comment: The traffic controller in this situation uses the main signal - arms down (“Chest, back - wall”). Trackless vehicles are allowed to move from the right and left sides - straight and to the right. According to markings 1.18, which organizes the direction of movement along the lanes, you can only turn right. But in the table of correct answers, answer No. 2 is correct. “Straight or to the right,” referring to paragraph 6.15 of the Traffic Regulations: “Drivers and pedestrians must comply with the requirements of signals and orders of the traffic controller, even if they contradict traffic light signals, the requirements of road signs or markings.” But this paragraph should be used by traffic controllers (including traffic police officers) not in the usual standard situation, but only in situations of necessity - in connection with an accident, the formation of a traffic jam, to organize the passage of convoys, special vehicles, etc. But you and I are preparing for the exam in the traffic police, therefore we recognize with all conventions the correctness of this answer, the basis of which is clause 6.15 of the traffic rules.
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: What should you do when making a left turn on a two-lane road?

answers.text: Start the maneuver while simultaneously turning on the left turn indicators
Turn on the left turn indicators, then proceed with the maneuver
Make sure it is safe to perform the maneuver, then turn on the left turn indicators and begin the maneuver.

questions.comment: On any road, when turning left or making a U-turn, you, as required by paragraph 8.1 of the traffic rules, turn on the left turn signal in advance. But since in the situation under consideration, there is one lane in each direction, one of the drivers moving behind you in the same direction, already ahead of you, may give a signal and begin overtaking. In this case, according to paragraph 11.3 of the traffic rules, by your actions you will create an obstacle to him, being an unconscious violator of the traffic rules. Therefore, on such a road, if the traffic is moving, smoothly reduce the speed in advance, while practically not braking, lightly pressing the brake pedal several times, turn on the brake lights; at this time, make sure that no one is overtaking, turn on the left turn signal and, once again making sure that further intentions to turn left or make a U-turn are clear to other drivers, proceed to perform the maneuver, taking into account oncoming traffic. (Paragraphs 8.1, 11.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to start moving from the sidewalk. Should you give way to a motorcycle making a U-turn?

answers.text: You shouldn't if you are driving a taxi.

questions.comment: Before driving, the driver must make sure that the maneuver will be safe and will not interfere with other road users. (Clause 8.1 of the Traffic Regulations). According to this clause, you give way to a motorcyclist, regardless of what vehicle you are driving.

questions.question: Is the driver of a car allowed to reverse to pick up a passenger in a tunnel?

answers.text: Permitted if it does not interfere with other traffic participants

questions.comment: Reversing is prohibited in tunnels. In this case, regardless of the presence of lighting in the tunnel, the lighting devices on the vehicle must be turned on. The actions of this driver should be regarded as dangerous. (Clause 8.11, 8.12 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: In this situation, you are allowed to move:

answers.text: On the right or middle lane

questions.comment: On any roads that have three or more lanes for traffic in a given direction, occupying the leftmost lane is allowed only during heavy traffic, when other lanes are occupied. You move alone. You can continue driving in the lane you are in, or change lanes to the far right. (Clause 9.4 of traffic rules)
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: Is overtaking allowed in the tunnel?

answers.text: Allowed only in the presence of artificial lighting

questions.comment: Overtaking is prohibited on bridges, overpasses, overpasses and under them, as well as in tunnels. (Clause 11.4 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Is it possible for the driver to park the car in this manner?

answers.text: It is possible, if it does not interfere with the movement of other vehicles.

questions.comment: Parking at an angle to the edge of the roadway is prohibited, with the exception of those places whose configuration allows for a different location (local widening of the roadway), indicated by appropriate signs and markings. (Clause 12.2 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: In what case are you required to give way to a truck?

answers.text: In both of the above cases

questions.comment: The intersection is controlled. You are allowed to move. When turning left or making a U-turn, you must give way to vehicles moving straight and to the right from the opposite direction. Yield to the truck in both of the listed cases. (Clause 13.3, 13.4 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: You intend to continue driving straight when the traffic light is flashing yellow. What are your actions?

answers.text: Stop and continue driving only when the traffic light turns green
Give way to a horse-drawn carriage
Pass the intersection first together with an oncoming car

questions.comment: An intersection with a flashing yellow traffic light is unregulated, in this case it is equivalent, since there are no priority signs. We are guided by the “right hand rule”, i.e. whoever has an obstacle on the right concedes. You have an obstacle on the right - you will be the last to cross the intersection, giving way to a horse-drawn cart. (Clause 13.3, 13.11 of the Traffic Rules)

questions.question: You intend to turn left. Who do you have to give way to?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles on the main road have priority and are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves. After they pass, guided by the same rule, vehicles on the secondary road will pass. You pass first, without yielding to anyone. The motorcyclist is second, the bus is third, the passenger car is last. (Clause 13.9, 13.1, 13.11 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: In what case is the driver of a vehicle approaching an unregulated pedestrian crossing obliged to give way to pedestrians?

answers.text: If pedestrians enter the roadway (tram tracks) to cross
In both of the above cases

questions.comment: The driver of a vehicle approaching an unregulated pedestrian crossing must comply with the requirements to “give way.” This requirement must be met in both of the listed cases. (Clause 14.1 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Pedestrian crossings and stops of fixed-route vehicles

questions.question: Should you switch the high beam to low beam if the driver of an oncoming vehicle periodically switches the headlights to indicate the need for this?

answers.text: Must only if the distance to the oncoming vehicle is less than 150 m

questions.comment: The periodic switching of headlights is a kind of request to you by the driver of an oncoming car to switch the lights on your vehicle in order to avoid blinding.(Clause 19.2 of the SDA, "Vehicle Control Technique")
topic: Use of external lighting fixtures and audible signals

questions.question: What administrative penalty can be imposed on the driver of a vehicle for leaving the scene of a traffic accident in which he is a participant in violation of the Rules?

answers.text: Only a fine of 1000 to 1500 rubles
A fine of 1,000 to 1,500 rubles or deprivation of the right to drive vehicles for a period of 1 to 1.5 years
Deprivation of the right to drive vehicles for a period of 1 to 1.5 years or administrative arrest for a period of up to 15 days

questions.comment: According to Art. 12.27 part 2, the driver of a vehicle for leaving, in violation of the Rules, the scene of a traffic accident in which he is a participant, is subject to administrative punishment - deprivation of the right to drive a vehicle for a period of 1 to 1.5 years or administrative arrest for a period of up to 15 days. “Code of the Russian Federation on Administrative Offenses”

questions.question: To prevent a vehicle with a manual transmission from rolling away during a short stop on an uphill slope, you should:

answers.text: Engage first gear or reverse gear
Move the gear shift lever to neutral position

questions.comment: When stopping briefly on an incline, the parking brake should be applied on a vehicle with a manual transmission.

questions.question: Does the choice of lateral interval depend on the speed of travel?

answers.text: The choice of lateral interval does not depend on the speed of movement
When driving speed increases, the lateral interval must be increased
When driving speed increases, the lateral interval can be reduced

questions.comment: Any vehicle structurally has a “dynamic corridor”, i.e. its lateral deviation from linear motion. The “traffic corridor” is especially large for long vehicles and vehicle combinations. As the speed increases, it is necessary to increase the lateral interval with both passing and oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: A driver’s license confirming the right to drive vehicles of category “A” also confirms the right to drive vehicles:

answers.text: Subcategories "B1" with motorcycle landing or motorcycle-type steering wheel

questions.comment: According to Article 25, Clause 7 of the Federal Law “On Road Safety”, a driver’s license confirming the right to drive vehicles of category “A” also confirms the right to drive all listed vehicles.

questions.question: Which of the following signs informs you that you are approaching the beginning of a section of road with oncoming traffic?
questions.comment: Only warning sign “A” - 1.21 “Two-way traffic” - is installed in front of a roadway with oncoming traffic if it was preceded by a section of road with one-way traffic. Sign “B” - 5.8 “Reversible traffic” - informs about the beginning of a section of the road on which on one or more lanes the direction of movement can change to the opposite. Sign “B” - 5.15.7 “Direction of traffic along lanes” - indicates the organization of traffic in both directions on a three-lane road. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Are you allowed to drive to your place of work located within the coverage area of ​​these signs?
questions.comment: Sign 8.5.2 “Working days” indicates that sign 3.2 “No traffic” is valid only on weekdays. But since those who live, work or serve enterprises located in the area of ​​the sign can deviate from the actions of this sign, you are allowed to drive “under the sign” on any day of the week. (“Road Signs”)

questions.question: What does this road sign with a yellow background inform you about?

answers.text: Further movement is possible only in the second lane
Further movement is only possible on the carriageway in the opposite direction
Further movement is only possible on another road

questions.comment: Sign 6.19.1 “Preliminary indicator for changing lanes onto another carriageway” indicates the direction of the detour of a section of the roadway closed to traffic on a road with a dividing strip. The yellow background of the sign indicates that the detour is temporary. (“Road Signs”)

questions.question: Are you allowed to cross a double solid horizontal line?

answers.text: Allowed only when leaving courtyards and other adjacent areas

questions.comment: Double continuous horizontal markings 1.3 separating traffic flows in opposite directions are PROHIBITED in all cases. (“Horizontal markings”)

questions.question: What do the arrows on a green traffic light inform you about?

answers.text: Right turns are always prohibited at this intersection.
Movement to the right is regulated by an additional section
This intersection allows left turns from two lanes.

questions.comment: Black contour arrows placed on the main green traffic light inform drivers about the presence of an additional section of the traffic light and indicate other permitted directions of movement than the additional section signal. (Clause 6.4 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: Such a hand signal given by the driver of a passenger car informs you:

answers.text: About his intention to start a movement
About the danger around the corner

questions.comment: The left hand extended to the side is a left turn signal, which the driver must give before starting to move. (Clause 8.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: In which direction is the driver of a car allowed to continue driving?
questions.comment: As an exception, entry to a roundabout intersection can be made from any lane in that direction (without first changing lanes). Departure from this intersection is carried out according to the general rules. To turn right, you must take the appropriate extreme position on the roadway in advance. When making a turn, the vehicle should move as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway. The trajectory of the truck corresponds to the above. The driver of a passenger car can only continue driving in a circle. (“Road signs”, paragraphs 8.5, 8.6 of traffic regulations).

questions.question: You can continue driving at the intersection:
questions.comment: U-turns are not prohibited at intersections. In this situation, you can continue driving in any direction. (Clause 8.11 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Driving in a populated area at a speed of more than 60 km/h is permitted:

answers.text: Only if there are road signs allowing driving at speeds over 60 km/h
In both of the above cases

questions.comment: In populated areas, the speed is limited: it should not exceed 60 km/h. Increased speed can be introduced on certain sections of roads by installing signs 3.24 “Maximum speed limit.” (Clause 10.2 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: In this situation, the advantage is:

answers.text: Passenger car as it moves uphill
Truck, as the obstacle is in the lane of a passenger car

questions.comment: If it is difficult to pass oncoming traffic on slopes indicated by the corresponding signs 1.13 “Steep descent”, 1.14 “Steep ascent”, the driver of the vehicle moving downhill must give way. In this traffic situation, the truck driver yields. The driver of a passenger car has an advantage because he is moving uphill. (Clause 11.7 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Can you park your car at the specified location?

answers.text: Only possible if road visibility is at least 100m

questions.comment: If there is a ramp on the side of the road, you can also park the car in places with limited visibility. (Clause 12.1, 12.4, 12.5 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: What should you do when turning left?

answers.text: Stop at the stop line and wait for the traffic controller's signal to allow the turn.
Having arrived at the intersection, stop and wait for the traffic controller's signal to allow the turn.
Turn, giving way to an oncoming car

questions.comment: The intersection is controlled. The traffic controller has his hands down. Trackless vehicles are allowed to move straight and to the right from the right and left sides. You intend to turn left. Therefore, you need to stop in front of the stop line and wait for the traffic controller’s signal corresponding to your intention, and then perform the maneuver. (Clause 6.10, 6.13, 13.3 of the Traffic Regulations, “Horizontal markings” 1.12)

questions.question: You intend to drive through the intersection in the forward direction. What are your actions?

answers.text: Pass the intersection together with the tram, without giving way to a truck
Drive through the intersection, giving way to a truck

questions.comment: The intersection is equivalent. A tram at equivalent intersections has an advantage over trackless vehicles regardless of its further direction of movement. Trackless vehicles are guided by the "right-hand rule", i.e. those who have a hindrance on the right, give way. You have an obstacle on the right – you give way to the truck.(Clause 13.11 of the Traffic Rules)

questions.question: Who do you have to give way to when driving straight?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles on the main road have priority and are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves. After them, guided by the same rule, vehicles on the secondary road pass through the intersection. The motorcyclist will pass first, the bus will pass second, and the car will pass third. You are the last, giving way to all vehicles. (Clause 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 Traffic Rules)

questions.question: Is driving instruction allowed on this road?

answers.text: Allowed only when driving in the far right lane of the roadway

questions.comment: Traffic follows sign 5.1 on the motorway. Training driving on it is not prohibited, i.e. allowed. (Clause 16.1 of the Traffic Regulations).

questions.question: Is it possible to use fog lights instead of low beam headlights during daylight hours?

answers.text: Possible, except when driving in tunnels and in poor visibility conditions

questions.comment: Permitted during daylight hours, except when driving in tunnels and in conditions of poor visibility. (Clause 19.4, 19.5 of traffic rules)
topic: Use of external lighting fixtures and audible signals

questions.question: Is it allowed to install tires with different tread patterns on the same axle of a passenger car?

answers.text: Allowed only on the rear axle

questions.comment: Tires with different tread patterns behave differently due to uneven traction between the wheels and the road. The consequence of this difference can be the car skidding both when moving along a curved path and when braking. (“Basic provisions”, “List of faults” clause 5.8)
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: In the event of loss of wheel traction due to the formation of a “water wedge”, the driver should:

answers.text: Reduce speed by sharply pressing the brake pedal

questions.comment: Water sliding - or so-called aquaplaning - occurs when driving a passenger car in heavy rain or when driving through accumulations of water on the road in lowlands: in autumn, spring or during a thaw. Being aware of this phenomenon, the driver should not be taken by surprise. There can only be one piece of advice - immediately reduce the speed by applying engine braking. “Driving techniques”

questions.question: How does a driver's fatigue affect his attention and reaction?

answers.text: Attention and reaction time do not change

questions.comment: Fatigue and tiredness undoubtedly affect traffic safety. Attention weakens, reaction time increases. A good driver should take pauses in movement, which from time to time will interrupt the monotony of driving. A few minutes are often enough to restore the level of attention necessary for safe movement. (“Driving School”, A.I. Kopusov-Dolinin, EKSMO Publishing House)

questions.question: At the request of which persons are drivers required to undergo an examination for alcohol intoxication and a medical examination for intoxication?

answers.text: Officials authorized to exercise federal state control (supervision) in the field of road safety

questions.comment: The driver is required to undergo an alcohol intoxication examination and a medical intoxication examination at the request of officials who are granted the right of state supervision and control over road safety and vehicle operation. (Clause 2.3.2 Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Which of the following signs informs you that at an intersection you must give way to vehicles approaching from the left?
questions.comment: The order of passage of vehicles at intersections is determined by the priority signs indicated in this case "A" and "B".The sign "A" – 2.3.3 "Junction of a secondary road" – informs that the adjacent road on the left is secondary. Moving along the main road, you have an advantage. The combination of signs "B" – 2.4 "Give way" with the sign 8.13 "Direction of the main road" informs that moving vehicles located on the main road on the left and directly from the opposite direction have an advantage. You are obliged to give way to them. Sign "B" – 5.13.1 "Exit to the road with a lane for fixed-route vehicles" – is included in the group of signs of special regulations. It cannot regulate the order of passage of vehicles.(“Traffic Signs”)

questions.question: Are you allowed to continue driving in a straight direction when driving a car with a trailer?

answers.text: Allowed if you live in the area indicated by the sign

questions.comment: Sign 3.7 “No driving with trailers” prohibits driving with trailers only on trucks and tractors. It does not apply to passenger cars with a trailer. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: You are allowed to move:

answers.text: In any of the directions indicated

questions.comment: Sign 5.7.2 “Entering a one-way road” prohibits turning right, i.e. oncoming traffic. The permitted directions of movement at such an intersection are straight, left (in the direction of the arrow on the sign) and a U-turn. You can continue driving in any of the directions indicated. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: What does increasing the stroke length of a dashed marking line inform you about?

answers.text: About the beginning of the zone where any maneuvers are prohibited
About the beginning of a dangerous section of the road
On approaching a solid marking line dividing traffic flows in the same direction

questions.comment: Marking 1.6 (the approach line is a broken line with the length of the strokes three times longer than the spaces between them) warns of approaching the solid line 1.1 (maybe 1.11), which separates traffic flows, in this case, passing directions. (“Horizontal markings”)

questions.question: Can you change lanes into the next lane?

answers.text: Yes, if the truck is moving at a speed of 30 km/h

questions.comment: To perform the maneuver, you would be forced to enter the reversible lane. The red signal of the reversing traffic light prohibits movement in this lane. (Clause 6.7 of the Traffic Regulations, “Horizontal markings”)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: Are you required to turn on the right turn signals before entering this intersection?

answers.text: Obligated only in the presence of vehicles moving behind

questions.comment: When entering the roundabout, you make a right turn. You should inform other road users about this by turning on the right direction indicators.(Clause 8.1 of SDA)

questions.question: When leaving the adjacent territory, you must give way to:

answers.text: Vehicles, persons using personal mobility devices and pedestrians

questions.comment: When entering the road from the adjacent territory, the driver must give way to: vehicles, persons using personal mobility devices and pedestrians. (Clause 8.3 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Is it permissible to make a U-turn on a section of the road marked with this sign?

answers.text: Allowed only when road visibility is at least 100 m

questions.comment: By making a U-turn on a road marked with sign 5.5 “One-way road”, you will make oncoming traffic, which is unacceptable on this road. (“Road Signs”)

questions.question: In what cases is a driver prohibited from driving at a speed of more than 50 km/h?

answers.text: If the corresponding prohibition is set by the road sign “Maximum speed limit”
In all of the above cases

questions.comment: In all of the above cases, the driver is prohibited from driving at a speed of more than 50 km/h (Clause 1.2, term “Moped”, 10.4 Traffic Rules, sign 3.24 “Maximum speed limit”)

questions.question: Is overtaking allowed at a pedestrian crossing?

answers.text: Prohibited only if there are pedestrians on it

questions.comment: Overtaking is prohibited at pedestrian crossings. (Clause 11.4 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Where can you stay?
questions.comment: Outside a populated area, stopping or parking is permitted only on the right side of the road - on the side of the road, and in its absence - at the edge of the roadway. You will do the right thing if you stop at place “B”. (Clause 12.1 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: What should you do when turning left?

answers.text: Give way only to a truck with a flashing light on

questions.comment: The intersection is controlled. Priority signs don't work. A truck with a “yellow flashing light” stands and waits for a traffic light signal allowing it to move, since a special yellow signal does not allow deviating from the requirements of traffic lights. When turning left, you must give way to vehicles moving directly from the opposite direction. Give way to the bus. (Clause 3.4, 13.3, 13.4 Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to turn around. What are your actions?

answers.text: Be the first to turn around
Drive to the intersection and, giving way to a passenger car, complete a U-turn
You will act by mutual agreement with the driver of the car

questions.comment: The intersection is equal. When determining the order of passage through an intersection, drivers are guided by the “right-hand rule.” During a turn, you will see an obstacle on the right, give way. (Clause 13.11 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Who do you have to give way to when driving straight?
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles located on the main road have an advantage, while trackless vehicles are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves, yielding to a tram that is in equal conditions with them. You give way to a tram and a car, which will pass the intersection at the same time, since their trajectories do not intersect. The motorcyclist is inferior to everyone because he is on a secondary road. (“Road signs”, paragraphs 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Is it permitted to drive on the highway in a vehicle whose technical speed is less than 40 km/h?

answers.text: Allowed only in the far right lane

questions.comment: The movement of vehicles whose speed, according to their technical characteristics or their condition, is less than 40 km/h is prohibited on highways (Clause 16.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Carriage of cargo is prohibited if it:

answers.text: Protrudes more than 1 m beyond the dimensions of the vehicle at the front or rear and is marked with identification marks
Covers external lighting devices, retroreflectors, registration and identification plates

questions.comment: According to clause 23.3 of the traffic rules, the carriage of goods is prohibited under the conditions listed in the second answer. When cargo protrudes more than 1 m beyond the dimensions of the vehicle in front or behind, transportation is not prohibited. But in this case, the cargo must be marked with the identification sign “Large vehicle”, and in the dark and in conditions of insufficient visibility with lighting devices. (Clause 23.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Is it permissible to drive a vehicle to a repair or parking site in the dark with the headlights and tail lights not lit (due to a malfunction)?

answers.text: Allowed only on roads with artificial lighting

questions.comment: In the event of this malfunction, in the dark or in conditions of insufficient visibility, movement to both the repair site and the parking area is strictly prohibited, regardless of the availability of road lighting. (Clause 2.3.1 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Malfunctions and conditions for admitting vehicles to operation

questions.question: When turning left, traffic safety is achieved by turning along the trajectory shown:
questions.comment: If the parameters (mass and speed) of moving cars in both figures are the same, then the centrifugal force tending to skid the car is theoretically less in the right figure, because the trajectory of movement passes along a larger radius of curvature. But the driver has no reserve (he exits the turn at the very edge of the roadway), and all the factors affecting the car cannot always be taken into account. The trajectory shown in the left figure is preferable, because in this case, there is a margin in the width of the roadway, and the speed should be significantly reduced before entering the turn. (“Driving techniques”)

questions.question: How to ensure restoration of the victim's airway when preparing him for cardiopulmonary resuscitation?

answers.text: Lay the victim on his back on a hard surface, tilt his head back, place one hand on his forehead, lifting his chin with two fingers of the other hand.
Lay the victim on his side, tilt his head to his chest. If there is mucus and vomit, clean the mouth from them.
Lay the victim on his back and, without throwing his head back, squeeze his cheeks to spread his lips and open his mouth. If there is mucus and vomit, clean the mouth from them.

questions.comment: Since the victim, lying unconscious on his back, may die from suffocation as a result of the fall of the tongue, it is necessary to ensure the patency of the respiratory tract. Lay the victim on his back on a hard surface, tilt his head back, put one hand on his forehead, lifting his chin with two fingers of the other hand.

questions.question: What maneuver does the driver of a car intend to perform?
questions.comment: The driver of a passenger car “changes lanes” into a parallel lane and further “advances” - the vehicle moves at a speed greater than the speed of the passing vehicle.

questions.question: This sign:

answers.text: Shows traffic directions at the intersection
Indicates that the road being crossed has two lanes of traffic.
Prohibits making a U-turn at an intersection

questions.comment: Warning sign 1.34.3 "Direction of turn" indicates the direction of movement at the T-junction.(“Traffic Signs”)

questions.question: A truck with a permissible maximum weight of not more than 3.5 tons can travel at the following speeds:
questions.comment: The plate under the sign 8.4.1 “Type of vehicle” extends the sign to trucks, including those with a trailer, with a permissible maximum weight of more than 3.5 tons. Your car does not belong to them, continue driving at the speed you are allowed - no more than 90 km/h, since the action takes place outside the populated area. (“Road signs”, clause 10.3 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Which sign indicates the length of the turnaround zone?
questions.comment: Sign “B” – 6.3.2 “U-turn zone” is used to indicate the place on the road section that allows a turn, and its length. In this case, the length of the turnaround zone is no more than 15 m. The combination of signs “A” - 6.3.1 “Place for a turn” and plate 8.1.1 “Distance to object” indicate that 50 m from the installation of signs in the direction of travel there will be a place intended only for making a turn. The length of the turning zone in this situation is not specified. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: This markup means:

answers.text: A section of the road where driving near the sidewalk is prohibited
Places where any stopping is prohibited

questions.comment: Yellow zigzag markings 1.17.1 indicate stopping places for route vehicles and taxi ranks. (“Horizontal markings”)

questions.question: In what cases is it necessary to give way to a vehicle that has special color schemes applied to its external surfaces?

answers.text: If his driver turned on a blue flashing light and a special sound signal
If his driver turned on the blue flashing light

questions.comment: To gain an advantage, the “operative” must turn on a blue flashing light and a special sound signal. (Clause 3.1 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Does signaling with turn signals give you an advantage in traffic?
questions.comment: Signaling with direction indicators does not give the driver an advantage and does not exempt him from taking precautions.(Clause 8.2 of the Traffic Rules)

questions.question: Are you allowed to make a right turn along the indicated trajectory in this situation?
questions.comment: When turning right, the vehicle should move as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway, i.e. in the far right lane. In this case, you do not have such an opportunity due to the car stopping in this lane. Continue moving along the indicated trajectory. (Clause 8.6 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Can you make a U-turn?
questions.comment: You are on a one-way road on which oncoming traffic is prohibited. You cannot continue driving along the indicated trajectories. (“Road signs” 5.6, 1.21)

questions.question: In what cases is it prohibited to drive in the lane intended for oncoming traffic on dual carriageway roads?

answers.text: If it is separated by tram tracks
If it is separated by a dividing strip
If it is separated by dividing markings 1.1 or 1.3, or markings 1.11, the broken line of which is located on the left
In all of the above cases

questions.comment: On any two-way roads, it is prohibited to drive in a lane intended for oncoming traffic if it is separated by tram tracks, a dividing strip, marking 1.1, marking 1.3 or marking 1.11, the broken line of which is located on the left. (Clause 9.1(1) Traffic Regulations) Changes in traffic regulations from July 12, 2017.
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: Are you allowed to overtake a truck at the end of a hill?

answers.text: Permitted if the speed of the truck is no more than 30 km/h

questions.comment: Fracture of the road limits visibility at the end of the climb. Therefore, overtaking is prohibited.(Clause 11.4 of the SDA)Do not forget the main condition for overtaking - "The path necessary for overtaking should never exceed half of the visible segment of the path."

questions.question: Are you allowed to park your car in this place if there is a narrow shoulder?
questions.comment: Parking outside populated areas on the roadway marked with sign 2.1 “Main Road” is prohibited. (Clause 12.5 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: What should you do when turning right?

answers.text: Give way only to tram A
Give way only to tram B

questions.comment: To turn right you must cross the tram tracks. Both trams, just like you, have the right to move; they move “in the hands of the traffic controller.” You give way to them, since with the simultaneous right to travel, the tram has an advantage over trackless vehicles. (Clause 6.10, 13.6 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to turn left. What are your actions?

answers.text: Enter the intersection first and, giving way to the motorcycle, complete the turn

questions.comment: The intersection is equal. Drivers follow the “right-hand rule” among themselves. You start moving first, because at the initial moment there is no obstacle on the right. Having rolled out to the intersection, you stop just before turning left, since there is a motorcycle to your right along the trajectory of movement. Once the motorcycle has passed, you can complete the maneuver. The passenger vehicle will be the last to cross the intersection. (Clause 13.11 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: You are required to give way when driving straight:
questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles located on the main road have priority, which are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves. You are on a secondary road, give way to both vehicles. (“Road signs” 2.4, 8.13; clauses 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 of the traffic rules)

questions.question: Which drivers are breaking the rules?

answers.text: Drivers of a truck with a permissible maximum weight of 3 tons and a moped

questions.comment: Mopeds are prohibited on the highway. It is also prohibited for trucks with a r.m.m. of more than 2.5 tons to move on any road that has three lanes in a given direction in the leftmost lane. Drivers of trucks and mopeds violate the rules (Clauses 9.4, 16.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: When dazzled by the high beam headlights of oncoming or passing vehicles, the driver must:

answers.text: Move right to the edge of the roadway and stop
Turn on the hazard warning lights and, without changing lanes, reduce speed and stop

questions.comment: Try to perform the actions in the sequence specified by the Rules – turn on the alarm and, without changing lanes, slow down and stop.(Clause 19.2 of the Traffic Rules)
topic: Use of external lighting fixtures and audible signals

questions.question: What types of administrative penalties can be applied to drivers for violations of the Rules?

answers.text: Warning, fine, deprivation of the right to drive vehicles, administrative arrest
Warning, fine, deprivation of the right to drive vehicles, confiscation of the instrument of commission or the subject of an administrative offense, administrative arrest, compulsory work

questions.comment: According to Chapter 12 of the Code of Administrative Offences, all types of punishments listed in the answers may be applied to drivers for violating traffic rules. The correct answer is the most complete. “Code of the Russian Federation on Administrative Offences”

questions.question: What driver actions will lead to a decrease in the centrifugal force generated when turning?
questions.comment: The most effective quantity influencing centrifugal force is speed. It is proportional to the square of the speed. At the same time, the speed is determined by the driver. Its decrease leads to a decrease in centrifugal force. That is why it is recommended to reduce your speed before entering a turn. (“Driving Techniques”)

questions.question: How does alcohol affect a driver's reaction time?

answers.text: Alcohol does not affect reaction time

questions.comment: The driver behind the wheel requires not only a reaction, which increases when drinking alcohol. The most important thing is to constantly assess events and predict their development. Under the influence of alcohol, the brain makes incorrect assessments, and this is the main danger of driving while intoxicated. “Transport Psychology.”

questions.question: The main road is shown:

answers.text: Only in the top left picture
Only in the top right picture

questions.comment: In the top left picture, the main road is indicated by sign 5.1 "Motorway". In the upper right picture there is sign 2.3.2 “Junction of a secondary road.” (“Road signs”)

questions.question: At what distance to a slippery section of the road is this sign installed in a populated area?

answers.text: Just before the start of the slippery section

questions.comment: In populated areas, most warning signs are installed at a distance of 50-100 m from the dangerous area. At this distance, sign 1.15 “Slippery road” is also installed. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: Stopping in the area covered by this sign is permitted:

answers.text: Only taxis with the taximeter on
Only for vehicles with the “Disabled” identification badge installed.

questions.comment: If sign 3.27 “Stopping is prohibited” with sign 8.18 “Except for disabled people” is used, motorized strollers and cars marked with the “Disabled” sign can stop in its coverage area in accordance with the Federal Law.

questions.question: Which of the following signs are used to indicate camping?
questions.comment: Service signs inform about the location of the relevant objects. Designated signs: “B” – 7.10 “Camping”; “A” – 7.9 “Hotel or motel”; “B” – 7.11 “Recreation place”. (“Road signs”)

questions.question: If the reversing traffic lights are turned off, you should:

answers.text: Immediately change lanes to the right into the adjacent lane
Continue along the lane until the intersection
If there are no oncoming vehicles, continue driving along the lane

questions.comment: When the signals of the reversing traffic light, which is located above the lane marked on both sides by markings 1.9, are turned off, entry into this lane is prohibited. You need to change lanes to the right lane. (Clause 6.7 of the Traffic Regulations, “Horizontal markings”)

questions.question: You are allowed to continue driving:
questions.comment: Both the burning arrow of the additional section of the traffic light, and the sign 5.15.1 “Directions of traffic along the lanes”, and the markings allow you to make a left turn from the extreme left lane and a U-turn to move in the opposite direction. (“Road Signs”, paragraph 6.3 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Traffic lights and traffic controller signals

questions.question: How should a towed vehicle be marked if the hazard warning lights are missing or faulty?

answers.text: Install a warning triangle on the rear of the towed vehicle.
Turn on the rear fog light

questions.comment: If there is no or faulty hazard warning light on a towed motor vehicle, a warning triangle must be attached to its rear part. (Clause 7.3 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Use of hazard warning lights and warning triangles

questions.question: Is it possible for the driver of a car in this situation to start driving from the sidewalk?

answers.text: It is possible, if it does not interfere with the truck

questions.comment: Before driving, turn on the turn signal in the appropriate direction. You can start driving only after making sure that it will be safe and will not interfere with other road users. (Clause 8.1 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: The driver accidentally passed the required entrance to the yard. Is he allowed to use reverse in this situation and then turn right?

answers.text: It is allowed if it does not interfere with the movement of route vehicles.

questions.comment: Reversing is prohibited at stopping points. Such a maneuver is prohibited for you in this situation, since you are going to perform it at the stopping place of route vehicles, which is indicated by sign 5.16 “Bus and trolleybus stopping place”, as well as zigzag yellow markings 1.17.1. (Clause 8.11, 8.12 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: Which moped driver took the correct position in the lane?
questions.comment: Moped drivers must move along the right edge of the roadway in a single file, or in the lane for cyclists. Moped drivers are allowed to move along the side of the road if this does not interfere with pedestrians. (Clause 9.4, 24.7 of the Traffic Rules)
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: Is it possible for you to continue driving in the middle lane after passing a car moving in the right lane?

answers.text: Only possible if there is no oncoming traffic

questions.comment: The middle lane in this situation is used for traffic in both directions. It is only intended for overtaking, passing, turning left or making a U-turn. Having finished overtaking, you need to change lanes to the far right lane. (Clause 9.3 of the Traffic Regulations). You carry out further movement in accordance with clause 9.4 of the traffic rules. “Outside populated areas, vehicle drivers should drive them as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway.” You have such an opportunity.
topic: Location of vehicles on the roadway

questions.question: Which car drivers violated the stopping rules?
questions.comment: Stopping is prohibited - at pedestrian crossings and closer than 5 m in front of them. The driver of car “A” is clearly violating the rules, because stands close to the pedestrian crossing. The driver of car “B” stopped behind a pedestrian crossing, which does not contradict the Rules. In a populated area, as in this situation, you can stop on the left side of the road, if there are no tram tracks in the middle of the roadway. But because The traffic on this road is two-way, the driver of car “B” also violates the Rules by placing the car close to the pedestrian crossing. (Clause 12.1, 12.2 and 12.4 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: What should you do when moving in a forward direction?

answers.text: Wait for another signal from the traffic controller

questions.comment: The intersection is controlled. Trams move only “in the direction of the traffic controller’s hands,” i.e. directly. The tram driver is prohibited from turning right. Accordingly, he stands and waits for the traffic controller’s signal to change. You can continue moving straight or to the right. Pass the intersection first. (Clause 6.10 of traffic rules)

questions.question: Who do you have to give way to when turning left?
questions.comment: The intersection is equal. Drivers are guided by the “right hand rule”. The only obstacle on your right is a car, so you must give way to it. (Clause 13.11 of the Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: You intend to turn left. What are your actions?

answers.text: Give way only to passenger cars
Give way only to the bus

questions.comment: The intersection is unequal. The main road changes direction. Vehicles located on the main road have priority, which are guided by the “right-hand rule” among themselves. After they pass, vehicles on the secondary road pass. You are on a secondary road. Yield to both vehicles. (Clause 13.9, 13.10, 13.11 Traffic Regulations)

questions.question: The stop signal for the train driver is the following position of the hand or hands (in the daytime with a piece of bright material or some clearly visible object, at night - with a torch or lantern):
questions.comment: The stop signal for the train driver is a circular movement of the hand (in the daytime with a piece of bright material or some clearly visible object, at night - with a torch or lantern). (Clause 15.5 of the Traffic Rules. Note)

questions.question: In a tunnel with artificial lighting the following must be included:

answers.text: Low beam headlights or side lights
Low beam headlights or daytime running lights

questions.comment: Regardless of the illumination of the tunnel, when entering it, the high or low beam headlights must be turned on. (Clause 19.1 of the Traffic Regulations)
topic: Use of external lighting fixtures and audible signals

questions.question: Criminal liability is provided for driving a vehicle that does not cause serious harm to health or death of a person by a person in a state of intoxication, if he has previously been subject to administrative punishment:

answers.text: For failure to comply with the legal requirement of an authorized official to undergo a medical examination for intoxication
For committing any of the listed offenses

questions.comment: According to Article 264.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, criminal liability is provided in this situation for the commission of any of the listed offenses.

questions.question: When driving on a two-lane road behind a truck, you have the opportunity to overtake. What are your actions?

answers.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle you are overtaking, then change lanes into oncoming traffic and complete the maneuver
Change lanes into oncoming traffic, then approach the vehicle you are overtaking and complete the maneuver

questions.comment: The heavy truck ahead is a “moving wall” that limits your visibility. Only at a distance can you see the distance sufficient for overtaking, inform in a timely manner and be noticed by the overtaken. If necessary, stop overtaking in a timely manner and return to your lane. (“Driving techniques”)

questions.question: How is cardiopulmonary resuscitation performed on a victim?

answers.text: Artificial respiration and manual pressure on the victim’s sternum: first, 1 breath using the “mouth to mouth” method, then 15 pressures on the sternum
Hand pressure on the victim’s sternum and artificial respiration: first 15 pressures on the sternum, then 1 breath using the “mouth to mouth” method
Hand pressure on the victim’s sternum and artificial respiration: first 30 pressures on the sternum, then 2 breaths using the “mouth to mouth” method

questions.comment: When performing cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the victim must lie on a hard surface. Resuscitation begins with manual pressure on the victim’s sternum. After 30 compressions on the sternum, artificial respiration is performed - 2 breaths using the “mouth to mouth” method. When performing artificial respiration, it is recommended to use the “Mouth-Device-Mouth” device included in the first aid kit.

questions.question: What does the term "Lack of Visibility" mean?

Road visibility less than 150 m at night
Road visibility is less than 300 m in conditions of fog, rain, snowfall, etc., as well as at dusk
